- **The cause.** `@sigma/layer-maplibre` 3.0.0 stores a node's graph position as its Mercator x and
  the container's height less its Mercator y. A change of height therefore moves every node by that
  many Mercator units, about a hundred world-heights for 140 pixels, and the layer's own resize
  re-centres sigma before sigma has redrawn at the new projection. Turning the map's own size
  tracking off did not help; the flip itself is the fault (shown below).
- **The decision.** The layer is kept in the product as `apps/workspace/src/map/sigmaMaplibreLayer.ts`,
  with its y flipped about 1 instead of the container's height, and is otherwise the library's line
  for line. It is MIT-licensed, and its notice is in `NOTICE`. A fixed 3.x release does not exist,
  and 4.0 needs Sigma 4, which is held back (v0.4.0's notes). Moving to Sigma 4 is the time to drop
  the copy.
- **Tests.** `keyboard/map-view.spec.ts` with `keyboard/map-view-harness.tsx` draws three yards on
  the real map view in a browser, shrinks its box and expects the camera still on them. It was red
  on the library (-85.05). With the copy it passed. The height-based flip planted back in the copy
  turned it red again (-85.05), and was restored by md5. With the map's own size tracking left on,
  it stays green, so that setting is left as it was.
- **A second change, found checking the first live.** With the flip fixed, the camera stayed on the
  yards but stepped in by about one zoom level (17.5 to 18.6), so two of the three yards left the
  view. The layer's resize kept only the centre, then copied sigma's camera, still framed for the old
  size, onto the map. It now keeps the area shown, fitting the map back to its previous bounds, and
  once sigma has redrawn it takes sigma's camera from the map rather than the other way round.
  `keyboard/map-view.spec.ts` gains "keeps every drawn node in view". It was red (the yards outside
  the bounds) and green after. The library's order planted back turned it red again, and was
  restored by md5.
- **Not changed.** The resize observer and every other map behaviour.

## ADR-088 — Two social-network filters in the Metrics panel: a relationship-strength floor and a metric threshold, both dimming

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as four multiple-choice questions and answered in chat).

Context. The owner asked for "some of the social network analysis based filters" from the Wynyard Enron case study to be added to the Glass. That walk-through filters the graph in two ways: a relationship-strength slider that thins the network to its strongly linked core and shows who the influential people are, and a "cliquishness" anomaly metric that finds people whose neighbourhood is more tightly interlinked than normal, which removes the well-connected CEO and leaves a person worth pursuing. The Glass already computes seven metrics in its Metrics panel (degree, weighted degree, betweenness, eigenvector, PageRank, clustering coefficient and the Clique Metric, spec 02 §3.2) and ranks nodes by them, but nothing filtered the graph by one, and the canvas's strength floor was wired to a constant zero. Four questions were put: dim or hide; a value slider or a top-N; where the filters live; whether they are remembered.

Decision.

1. **Both filters dim, they never remove** (spec 02 §2 rule 2). A link whose weight is below the strength floor is dimmed, and a node is dimmed when it has links and none of them is strong enough; a node with no links at all is left alone. A node whose value of the chosen metric is below the threshold is dimmed, as is one the metric gave no value. The two add to each other and to the timeline's own dimming (ADR-087); the status bar's dimmed count is the union.
2. **A metric is chosen, then a slider sets the value.** The slider runs from the metric's smallest to its largest value in the working set, in a hundred steps; the values are fetched when the metric is chosen, through the same compute route the Ranking section uses.
3. **They live in the Metrics panel, as a third section, Filter**, beside Ranking and Communities (one section open at a time, a closed section fetching nothing, as ADR-070 has it). A *Clear filters* button appears once anything is set.
4. **Not remembered.** A filter belongs to the view; a reload returns to the full picture.

Not decided here. Expansions by collaborators and by thread from the same video, which belong with the Enron emails (the next record); a top-N control; applying a metric as node size (spec 02 §3.2 names it and it is not built); a histogram of the metric's values behind the slider.

Consequences. New `src/metrics/filters.ts` (the pure rule: `filterDimming`, `valueRange`, `NO_FILTER`); `MetricsPanel.tsx` gains the Filter section and an `onFilterChange` prop; `App.tsx` unions the three dimming sources and feeds the canvas and the status bar; `METRICS_PANEL_ACTIONS` gains two ids. Spec 02 §3.2 gains the paragraph. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, shown red first: `filters.test.ts` (7: nothing with no filter; weak links and stranded nodes dim; a node with no links is left alone; below-threshold and unvalued nodes dim; both at once; a metric not yet valued dims nothing; the value range) and the keyboard cases `filter-section-sets-a-strength-floor-by-keyboard` and `filter-section-dims-below-a-metric-value-by-keyboard` in `keyboard/metrics-panel.spec.ts`. **Not seen:** the filters on the live Enron case, where the strength slider should grow the network from the CEO outwards as the video shows.

## ADR-089 — The emails behind an Enron link: a count, a paged list, the message with its entities marked, and extraction on request into inferred nodes

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as seven multiple-choice questions over two rounds and answered in chat); built in three steps, each its own commit.

Context. On the Enron case a link between two addresses is one summarised `COMMUNICATED_WITH` edge standing for many emails (ADR-053 option A: an address is an `Endpoint`, every message is an analytics event on the pair's edge). The owner asked for "the option to expand the link to show the count of emails and then also show a selected set of emails so that I can inspect those", and, pointing at the Wynyard "Foreign Fighters" demonstration (2:42 to 2:58), for an opened message to show its usernames, email addresses, names and dates marked in the text and joined to the rest of the data, with "the tool extract[ing] probabilistic entities by applying the POLE model" and showing them on the canvas. Three facts shaped the design: the Enron loader kept only 300 characters of each body, and the corpus is real data admitted on the owner's machine only (ADR-053); the document view's highlighting reads extraction candidates attached to a document id, and Enron emails had no document; the extraction route and the review queue exist, so model output already arrives as inferred candidates a person confirms (rule 5).

Decision.

1. **The text is the event's excerpt, made big enough.** The Enron loader keeps 4,000 characters of a body (enough for nearly every business email whole) and marks a longer one `truncated`, so a reader knows when the excerpt is not the whole. No new storage, one re-seed of Enron. The owner declined storing every email as a Document node up front and reading bodies from the corpus folder on demand.
2. **A link's events are read a page at a time, newest first, with the total.** `EventFilter` gains `edge_ids`; `AnalyticsPort.list_events` is a paged read (fifty at a time, two hundred at most) with access control in the query, held to by the conformance suite; `GET .../links/{edge}/events` answers only to someone who can see the link, with the one `link_not_found` refusal for a hidden and a missing link alike (rules 3 and 4), and needs Viewer. In the Glass the link menu offers *Show emails (n)*, *n* being the link's record count, and the Inspector gains an **Emails** section with date, subject, direction and the first words of each, paged.
3. **Opening an email shows its text with the entities already extracted marked in place**, through the existing document view, under a document id derived from the message id; before extraction there are no marks and the text is plain.
4. **Extraction is on request.** An *Extract entities* button runs the existing extraction once for that email, with the Enron handling and the POLE profile. The results are candidates (inferred, rule 5) that appear in the review queue and are marked in the text; at the first extraction the email itself is written as a `Document` node, linked to its sender and recipient by `MENTIONED_IN` (the addresses appear in the message), and each accepted candidate is an inferred node with a `MENTIONED_IN` link to that Document, the shape the ontology already has, so the evidence trail from entity to email to addresses is on the canvas.

Not decided here. Expanding by thread and by collaborators, as the Wynyard Enron demonstration does (a later record); a browser upload route for other corpora; extraction of several emails at once; a Document node for an email nobody has extracted from.

Consequences. **Step 1 (this commit):** `EXCERPT_CHARS` 4,000 and `truncated` in `demo_fixtures/enron.py`; `EventFilter.edge_ids`, `EventListRequest`/`EventListResult`, `AnalyticsPort.list_events`, the DuckDB implementation; `services/api/link_events.py` and the route; spec 03's route line. Tests shown red first: the conformance cases `test_event_filter_edge_ids_restricts_to_events_on_those_links`, `test_list_events_is_newest_first_paged_and_says_how_many_there_are` and `test_unauthorised_list_events_matches_a_corpus_without_the_hidden_event`; `test_link_events.py` (a visible link's emails newest first with a total and the exact filter sent; an empty link; a hidden link and a missing link refuse identically and ask the store nothing); `test_the_excerpt_keeps_a_whole_business_email_and_says_when_it_cut_a_long_one`; the levels test's new row. **Step 2:** the Glass's menu entry, Emails section and email view. **Step 3:** *Extract entities*, the Document node and the inferred nodes on the canvas. **Not seen:** anything of this on the live Enron case until the owner re-seeds it.

Build note (4 October 2026). All three steps of ADR-089 are built. Step 3: `services/api/email_extraction.py` (the email becomes a `Document` node linked to both addresses at the first extraction, the existing extraction runs on its text under `email:<event id>`, an accepted finding is written as an `inferred` node with a `MENTIONED_IN` link to the Document, and both steps put what they wrote into the working set through `WorkingSetService.add_written` and publish the delta); routes `POST .../links/{edge}/events/{event}/extract` and `POST .../links/{edge}/events/{event}/candidates/{candidate}/accept`, both Editor, both behind the visible-link gate, with `email_not_found` for an event not on the link or a candidate not from the email; the model is the caller's or, left out, the deployment's local model (`CONFORMANCE_MODEL`, the one the local stack has pulled). In the Glass the opened email carries *Extract entities* and the findings with one *Accept* each, and the Inspector hands the deltas to the working set. Tests shown red first: `test_email_extraction.py` (the Document and its two links, the text and the pending candidates under the email's id, nothing of the model's in the graph; the caller's model; an accepted finding as an inferred node linked to the email, into the working set; a hidden and a missing link refuse identically and write nothing; an event off the link and a candidate from another email are not found), the levels test's two rows, `LinkEvents.test.tsx` (extraction offered only where the view can take the delta; findings listed; one accepted) and the keyboard cases `extract-entities-by-keyboard-lists-the-findings` and `accept-a-finding-by-keyboard`. **Not seen:** against the live model on an Enron email; the owner re-seeds Enron (`make seed-enron`) for the 4,000-character excerpts first.

## ADR-090 — Analyst-proposed relationship types: proposed in a case, usable wherever their links are seen, promoted by an administrator in the Glass into a live overlay on the ontology

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as eight multiple-choice questions over three rounds and answered in chat). This is step C of ADR-081. ADR-081 and its Amendments 1 and 2 are unchanged except where decision 4 below says otherwise.

Context. ADR-081 decision 5 lets an Editor propose a relationship type when none fits, kept in the control-plane store and usable at once in that investigation only, and lets an administrator promote it into "a new ontology version through the existing schema step". Amendment 1 made the administrator any holder of `osprey-admin`, kept a proposed type Probabilistic until that administrator reclassifies it, and left open whether the promotion screen is in the Glass or the Admin console. Three facts about the code shaped the questions. The ontology is the packaged `packages/ontology/default.yaml`, loaded once when the API starts (`services/api/app.py`, `app.state.ontology`) and applied to the graph by `GraphPort.apply_schema`; nothing stores ontology versions at run time, and a version bump flags every recipe pinned to the old version (spec 09 §4). The Admin console is a placeholder (`GET /admin` in `harness/webapp.py`). A link in the graph belongs to no case: a link an analyst changes is a shared edge (`link_changes` records the case, the edge does not), so a link of a type proposed in one case can come into view in another.

Decision.

1. **Promotion happens in the Glass.** A *Proposed types* list, shown only to a holder of `osprey-admin`, lists proposals with their name, ends, direction, colour, thickness, the proposing analyst, the case and the reason, and offers *Promote* and *Reject*, each with a reason. No Admin console is built for this.
2. **Promotion writes a live overlay, not a new `default.yaml`.** A promoted type is stored in the control-plane store as part of an **ontology overlay** and is in force at once in every case, with no redeploy. The ontology in force is `default.yaml` plus the overlay. **The ontology version does not change**: the overlay carries its own **overlay revision**, a whole number that starts at 0 and rises by one at every promotion, recorded in the promotion's audit row and returned with every read of the ontology. Recipes are not flagged, because adding a type changes nothing a recipe already writes (the reason ADR-079 gives for not moving the version).
3. **A branch takes its parent's proposals.** Branching a case (ADR-084) copies to the new case every proposal pending in the parent, so the links it copies keep their type and the type stays in its change form.
4. **A proposed type is usable wherever one of its links is in view (this widens ADR-081 decision 5).** A pending proposal is offered in the change form of the case that proposed it (or a branch of it, decision 3) and of any case whose view holds a link of that type, where it is drawn in its own colour and thickness and may be chosen like any type. ADR-081 said "in that investigation only"; the owner chose "fully usable" knowing that a proposal then travels with its links. What another case sees is the type's definition only (name, ends, direction, colour, thickness, and that it is analyst-defined and pending); the proposer's reason and the audit stay with the proposing case and the administrator.
5. **Whose proposals an administrator sees.** An `osprey-admin` holder lists and acts on proposals from cases in their own unit only, the limit ADR-052's administrator safety net already uses, applied in the store's query (rule 3). The same person may propose and promote (Amendment 1 item 1).
6. **An administrator chooses the basis at promotion.** Promotion asks for Direct or Probabilistic, with a reason, and this is the only way an analyst-proposed type becomes Direct. A type promoted as Direct does not turn its existing links solid: every link of that type already written is given the per-link `probabilistic` mark (ADR-081 Amendment 2) as part of the promotion, so a link is still never promoted to Direct by a person (ADR-081 decision 2); only links written afterwards by a loader that backs the type are Direct.
7. **Names.** A proposed name follows the ontology's own naming rule and is refused if it is already a type in `default.yaml` or the overlay (including `SAME_AS` and `NOT_SAME_AS`). Two cases may each propose the same new name; when one is promoted the administrator is shown the others of that name, which are then recorded as merged into it, and their links (which already carry the name) take the promoted definition.
8. **Storage of the links.** Proposing a type creates its edge type in the graph store so that links of it can be written. That is storage schema, not the ontology: the type is in neither `default.yaml` nor the overlay until promoted. A rejected proposal's links stay, shown as "unclassified type" and drawn dotted in the default colour, and new links of it are refused (ADR-081 Amendment 1 item 4).
9. **Access (rules 3 and 4).** Proposing needs Editor on the case. Listing a case's proposals needs Viewer. Listing, promoting and rejecting across cases needs `osprey-admin` and a proposal from the caller's own unit; a proposal from another unit answers exactly as one that does not exist. Every read path has an access-control test.

Not decided here. What happens at promotion to links of a same-name proposal whose ends do not fit the promoted definition (to be put to the owner when the build reaches it); whether an overlay type may be named in an Ingest Studio recipe (step D's territory); withdrawing a proposal by its own analyst before an administrator acts; demoting or removing a promoted type.

Consequences. The build is in three commits, each with its spec changes (spec 01 for the overlay and proposals, spec 03 for the routes, spec 02 for the Glass). **C1, the server:** a control-plane table for proposals (case, definition, reason, proposer, status pending, promoted, rejected or merged, decision, decider, basis chosen) and one for the overlay revision; the ontology a request uses is `default.yaml` plus the overlay at the current revision, plus the pending proposals the case may use (decision 4), read per case rather than from the single `app.state.ontology`; `GraphPort.apply_schema` is given the widened schema at the same ontology version, which its history (keyed by version today) must allow; routes to propose and list in a case, and to list, promote and reject as an administrator; `LinkChangeService` accepts a proposed type where decision 4 allows it; branching copies proposals. **C2, the change form:** *Define a new type…* in the ADR-080 form, the proposed type offered and drawn per decision 4, a keyboard case and registry id (rule 13). **C3, the administrator's list** in the Glass, with keyboard cases for *Promote* and *Reject*. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, each to be shown red first: a Viewer cannot propose; an Editor without `osprey-admin` cannot promote or reject; an administrator cannot see or act on a proposal from another unit, and it reads exactly as a missing one; a proposal is not offered in a case where none of its links is in view and the case did not propose or inherit it, and is offered once one of its links is in view; a branch inherits its parent's pending proposals; a name already in `default.yaml` or the overlay is refused; a pending proposal's links are drawn dotted and are never Direct; promotion as Direct leaves every existing link of the type probabilistic; promotion raises the overlay revision by one and leaves the ontology version and every recipe's pin unchanged; the overlay survives an API restart; a rejected type's links stay and a new link of it is refused.

### ADR-090, Amendment 1 (4 October 2026) — the four questions ADR-090 left open

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as four multiple-choice questions and one clarifying question, answered in chat). ADR-090 is unchanged except where it listed these as not decided.

Decisions.

1. **Same-name proposals whose links do not fit are renamed, not merged.** When an administrator promotes one proposal and another proposal of the same name has links whose ends do not fit the promoted definition, the administrator gives that other proposal a new name (unused in `default.yaml`, the overlay and every pending proposal) and promotes it as a type of its own. Every link of the renamed proposal is rewritten under the new name, and the case that proposed it sees the new name from then on. A link's type cannot be changed in place in the graph store, so each is rewritten as a link change is (ADR-080): a new link with the old one's endpoints, properties and per-link basis, the old link recorded as its previous one, and the rename recorded in the change history with the administrator's reason. ADR-090 decision 7's "recorded as merged" still applies to a same-name proposal whose links all fit.
2. **A recipe may name an overlay type promoted as Direct.** An Ingest Studio recipe may name a type in the overlay only if it was promoted as Direct; one promoted as Probabilistic is refused as step D refuses any Probabilistic type, and a pending, rejected, withdrawn or retired type is never accepted. The check runs when the recipe is saved and again when it runs (ADR-081 Amendment 1 item 7). Step D builds it.
3. **The proposer may withdraw a proposal.** Before an administrator acts, the analyst who proposed it, or any Author of the case, may withdraw it with a reason; the withdrawal is audited. Its links stay and are shown as "unclassified type", exactly as on rejection, and new links of it are refused.
4. **An administrator may retire a promoted type.** An `osprey-admin` holder retires a promoted type from their own unit's proposals with a reason. The overlay revision rises by one, as at promotion. The type's links stay and are shown as "unclassified type", new links of it are refused, and a recipe that names it is refused when saved and when run. Retiring removes nothing from the graph (rule 6) and does not change any link's stored basis.

Consequences. ADR-090's C1 gains the routes to withdraw (Editor and Author of the case, or the proposer) and to retire (`osprey-admin`, own unit), and the rename path at promotion; C3's administrator's list gains *Retire* and the rename step, each with a keyboard case (rule 13). Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, each to be shown red first: renaming a same-name proposal at promotion rewrites every one of its links under the new name with its basis kept and the old link recorded as previous, and refuses a name already in use; a withdrawn proposal's links stay and a new link of it is refused; only the proposer or an Author can withdraw, and a Viewer cannot; retiring raises the overlay revision by one, leaves every link of the type in the graph, and refuses a new link of it; an administrator cannot retire a type from another unit's proposal, and it reads as a missing one; a recipe naming a Probabilistic, pending, withdrawn or retired overlay type is refused at save and at run (step D).

### ADR-090, Amendment 2 (5 October 2026) — renaming by alias: each proposal's links under a label of their own, nothing rewritten; C1 as built

Status: accepted 5 October 2026 (owner's choice, put as one multiple-choice question when the build reached Amendment 1 item 1: "At promotion, how should links of another same-name proposal that don't fit be handled? A rewrite cannot see links under restricted handling." Answer: "Rename by alias"). ADR-090 and Amendment 1 are unchanged except where this says so.

Context. Amendment 1 item 1 renames a misfitting same-name proposal at promotion by rewriting each of its links, and ADR-090 decision 6 marks each existing link of a type promoted as Direct. Both are rewrites by the Conduit, and the Conduit reads the graph as some principal: a link under handling that principal may not see would be missed, leaving it under the old name or unmarked, with nothing to say so. Two same-name proposals also shared one stored label, so their links could not be told apart once one was renamed.

Decision.

1. **Each proposal's links are stored under a label of their own,** `<name>__<proposal id>`, declared to the graph store as a hidden type (`EdgeTypeDef.hidden`) so it accepts the writes, and never offered, listed or sent to the Glass. `OntologySchema.storage_aliases` maps each such label to the name its links read as: the proposal's own name while pending and after it is rejected, withdrawn or retired; the promoted name once promoted, merged or renamed. The adapter reads a stored label through that map, and a filter by a type matches every label that reads as it (`EdgeTypeDef.aliases`). **So no link is ever rewritten,** restricted ones included: renaming, merging and retiring change one mapping, and Amendment 1 item 1's rewrite is replaced by this. A type name may not contain `__`.
2. **Promoted as Direct means Direct from then on** (`EdgeTypeDef.direct_since`, replacing ADR-090 decision 6's per-link marks): `effective_basis` reads a link of that type written before `direct_since` as probabilistic. A person still never promotes a link to Direct (ADR-081 decision 2).
3. **A branch takes its parent's proposals by reading its lineage**, not by copying rows: a case is offered the pending proposals of itself and of every case up its branch family that the caller may see (`visible_ancestors`, ADR-084 Amendment 2). This is how ADR-090 decision 3 is built; it keeps one proposal per decision for the administrator, and decision 4 already offers a proposal wherever one of its links is in view. **The owner may overrule this to literal copies;** nothing else depends on it.
4. **A name the case is already offered is refused**, as well as one in the ontology: two pending proposals of one name in one case's change form could not be told apart.
5. **Rejecting and withdrawing do not move the overlay revision;** promoting (including merging) and retiring do, as ADR-090 decision 2 and Amendment 1 item 4 say.

As built (C1, the server). `services/api/link_types.py`: `LinkTypeProposal`, `compose_ontology` (the one function building the ontology in force), `LinkTypeService` (refresh, `case_types`, `type_named`, propose, withdraw, promote with merge and rename, reject, retire), the routes' bodies and `public_ontology`; `link_type_store.py` (Postgres, proposals and the revision; the two `*_authorized` reads bind `principal.org_unit`); `link_changes.py` writes a link changed to a pending type under its proposal's label and checks types against the case's own; the adapter's `naming.py` and `builders.py` read and filter by alias, and read an unaliased `<name>__<id>` label as `<name>` (a process that composed before the proposal was made); `WorkingSetService.visible_membership` (what is in view is what the caller can see, so a hidden link does not offer its type); routes in spec 03 §3.4 and §3.10; `/v1/ontology` strips hidden types and aliases. The service catches up when the store's revision is ahead of its own, so a decision made in another process is seen at the next read; a proposal made in another process is offered there at once (it is read per request) but its label is only declared to that process's adapter at its next refresh, which reads it under its name meanwhile (decision 1's fallback). Found and fixed on the way: retyping a Direct link to a Probabilistic type with no basis asked for was refused as "cannot be marked Direct", because the kept basis was the old link's (`test_retyping_a_direct_link_to_a_probabilistic_type_makes_it_probabilistic`, red first).

Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, each shown red first: `test_link_type_overlay.py` (6, red before `compose_ontology` existed); `test_link_type_service.py` (20: offered in its case and branch and nowhere else; offered where a link of it is in view and not where that link is hidden from the caller; each refused name; promotion raising the revision and leaving the version; another unit's administrator answered as missing; merge and rename; reject, withdraw and retire keeping the links' name; the overlay surviving a restart; a link changed to a pending type written under its own label, refused in another case, and correctable after rejection; red as an import error before the service existed); `test_link_type_routes.py` (6: levels, the administrator's role and unit, and `/v1/ontology` never sending a storage label, red with the raw ontology returned); `test_link_type_store.py` (4, on real Postgres); `tests/conformance/graph_port/test_type_aliases.py` (3, on real ArcadeDB: an alias read and filtered, the old name refused for new writes, and a composed proposal's label read as its name and then as its renamed type, red with the unaliased fallback removed). **Not built here:** the change form's *Define a new type…* (C2) and the administrator's list (C3).

### ADR-090, Amendment 3 (5 October 2026) — C2 and C3 as built: the change form defines a type, the top bar lists the unit's proposals

Status: a build record, no new decision. ADR-090 and its Amendments 1 and 2 are unchanged.

As built. **C2:** the change form's types are the case's (`GET .../link-types`, read by `App.tsx` when a case opens and after each proposal or decision, so the canvas names and draws a pending type too); **Define a new type…** (`linktypes/DefineLinkType.tsx`, its rules in `defineType.ts`) takes a name in sentence case and makes the ID from it, as ADR-091 has a type carry both; the ends are the link's own, and *Either way round* makes it undirected between both kinds of entity. **C3:** *Proposed types* in the top bar, for a holder of `osprey-admin` only (`linktypes/ProposedTypes.tsx`); the basis at promotion has no default; the new-ID box appears when the server refuses the name, rather than the Glass guessing which names will be refused. **Not built:** withdrawing from the Glass (the route is built and tested; spec 02 §3.1f says the form does not offer it), and reading the case's types again when an expansion brings a link of a pending type into view (it is named and drawn as one when the case is next read).

Tests: `linkTypesApi.test.ts` (8), `defineType.test.ts` (9, written with the module, so not shown red), `LinkChange.test.tsx` (3 new, red before the form offered the step), `ProposedTypes.test.tsx` (5, red before the component existed); keyboard (rule 13) `link-change.spec.ts`'s *define-a-new-type-by-keyboard-and-it-is-chosen* and `proposed-types.spec.ts` (5 actions in `PROPOSED_TYPES_ACTIONS`), written after the code they prove. Whole Glass suite 1,097 green; keyboard 167 green bar the known flaky `link-selection` pair.

### ADR-084, Amendment 2 (4 October 2026) — a branch reads the events behind the links it copied; the timeline's reads take the case gate

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices: "read the parent's" and "both in one change", put as multiple-choice questions after the owner could not open an email on a branch tab of the Enron case). ADR-084 is unchanged except where this says so; it was silent on events.

Context. The owner, on a branch tab ("Enron corpus · 2 selected"), right-clicked a `COMMUNICATED_WITH (1)` link and could not reach the email behind it. Branching copies the chosen nodes and the links between them into a new case (ADR-084 decision 1), but every event is stored under the case it was loaded into (`EventRecord.investigation_scope`), and every event read asked only for the case on screen. On a branch the emails, the extraction and the timeline therefore read nothing. Tracing it found a second fault: the timeline's routes (`POST /v1/analytics/histogram`, `cross-filter`, `first-seen`, `geobins`, `sightings`) carry their case in the request body and checked no case level at all, so any signed-in account could read any case's event counts, filtered only by the per-event handling rules, against ADR-052 §8.

Decision.

1. **A branch reads its parents' events on the links it holds, and copies none.** A read in a case also counts the events of each case up its branch family (`branched_from`, nearest first) that the caller may see at Viewer, but only events on a link the branch holds: the one link asked about for *Show emails* and an email's extraction, the branch's working set for the timeline. A parent the caller cannot see contributes nothing and is not mentioned. The adapter applies its access filter to every inherited event as to the case's own.
2. **The port says it.** `EventFilter.inherited` (`InheritedEvents`: `scopes`, `edge_ids`) carries the widening, compiled into the adapter's `WHERE` clause (rule 3). It is set only by the Conduit (`services/api/event_scope.py`); a value sent by a caller is discarded. `geocode_events`, which writes a case's own events, refuses it.
3. **The analytics routes take the case gate.** Each of the five routes gates `investigation_scope` exactly as `_authorized_at` gates a case in a path, at Viewer: a case with no level, in another unit or not there answers 404, a level too low 403, each audited.

Consequences. Changed: `schemas/analytics.py` (`InheritedEvents`, `EventFilter.inherited`), the DuckDB adapter's shared predicate and `geocode_events`, `services/api/event_scope.py` (new: `visible_ancestors`, `with_inherited`, `link_event_filter`), `link_events.py`, `email_extraction.py`, and `app.py` (`_authorize` split out of `_authorized_at`, `_case_event_filter`, the five routes); spec 03 §3.3 and spec 02 §3.1h. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, each shown red first: the conformance cases `test_inherited_events_count_only_on_the_links_the_branch_holds`, `test_inherited_events_obey_every_other_predicate`, `test_unauthorised_inherited_event_matches_a_corpus_without_it` (3 failed before the adapter change), `test_inherited_events_with_no_links_held_add_nothing`, `test_geocode_refuses_an_inherited_filter`; in `test_link_events.py` `test_a_branch_lists_the_emails_its_parent_holds_on_that_link` (red: the owner's empty list), a parent the analyst cannot see, and a case that is not a branch; in `test_email_extraction.py` an email extracted from a branch and one from an unseen parent (red: "email not found"), after its analytics fake was corrected to honour the case at all (it ignored it, so it could not have shown this defect: rule 15's fixture that accepts what the real store refuses); `test_analytics_case_routes.py` (new, 12 cases: another unit's case is 404 and reads nothing on each route, red as 200 on all five; a branch's read carries its parent and its links; a non-branch and an unseen parent carry none; a caller's own `inherited` is discarded, red as passed through). **Not seen:** on the owner's Enron branch; and the live Phase 8 scenario (`test_phase8_exit_over_the_wire.py`) reads a case `harness.apply` seeded, which now answers 404 if the analyst holds no level on it.

## ADR-091 — A link reads by its type's display name in sentence case, with a named count

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as two multiple-choice questions after the owner said the count was confusing and the link name in capitals strange: "can the link have ID and name, please name (in sentence case) for display").

Context. Every link on the canvas was labelled `${type} (${occurrences})`, for example "COMMUNICATED_WITH (1)": the ontology's key in capitals and a bare number in brackets with no unit. The same key appeared in the link menu's title, the node menu's *Show links* entries, the change form's type list, the change history and the Inspector. A relationship type had a `name` (the key stored on every link) and nothing meant for a person to read.

Decision.

1. **A relationship type may declare a `label`**: its display name, in sentence case ("Communicated with"). It is optional; a blank one is refused at load. `name` stays the key stored on every link and used by every recipe, route and query.
2. **Where no label is declared, the Glass derives one** from the name: lower case, underscores to spaces, first letter capitalised (`COMMUNICATED_WITH` reads "Communicated with"). Nothing in the default ontology needs a label for that to read well, so none is authored yet.
3. **The count is named by what it counts**: "Communicated with · 3 emails" where the link is between email addresses (the rule *Show emails* already uses, ADR-089), "· 1 record" / "· n records" otherwise, with a thousands separator.
4. **The key is shown in one place only**: the Inspector's *Type ID* row, under the display name. Every other place a person reads a type uses the display name.

Consequences. Changed: `EdgeTypeDef.label` and the ontology JSON Schema (`"pattern": "\\S"`); the regenerated TypeScript types; in the Glass, `canvas/linkLabel.ts` (new: `linkTypeName`, `linkCaption`), `nodeAttributes.ts` (an optional, lazily called `caption` in the edge render context), `GlassCanvas.tsx` (the caption, a per-type cache of display names, the menus), `LinkDetails.tsx` (*Type ID*), `LinkChange.tsx`, `linkChangeForm.ts`, `describeChange.ts`, `EdgeInspectionOverlay.tsx`, `App.tsx`; spec 01 §1.2 and spec 02 §4. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken: `test_relationship_basis.py`'s label cases (the two blank labels shown red with the schema's rule removed: before the field existed they were refused only because the schema refuses any unknown field, the wrong reason); `linkLabel.test.ts` (shown red before the module existed); the caption cases in `nodeAttributes.test.ts` (shown red against the old label, and one proving no caption is built for a link that is not labelled); five Glass unit expectations and one keyboard case moved from capitals to sentence case. `make glass-perf` fails two cases (first frame of the 50k/250k fixture and the pan/zoom sweep, a 60-second wait), **and fails them identically at the commit before this change**, so it was failing before; it had not been run since ADR-081 step A's edge programs, and is recorded as open. **Not seen:** the captions on the live Enron case.

### ADR-089, Amendment 1 (4 October 2026) — correction: extraction never found its email; an event is looked up by `event_ids`

Seen by the owner on the live Enron case: *Extract entities* did nothing. The API log shows `POST .../events/{event}/extract` answering 404 for an email whose link listed it a moment earlier; the model was never asked (Ollama holds `qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct`, served through LiteLLM, and is the deployment's default, `CONFORMANCE_MODEL`).

Cause. Step 3 looked the email up with `value_filters={"event_id": [...]}`. The DuckDB adapter reads a `value_filters` name it does not know as a key inside `properties` (`_field_expression`; `event_id` is a column, not one of `_TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS`), so the lookup matched nothing and every extraction answered `email_not_found`. Step 3's tests passed because their analytics stand-in matched `event_id` directly: a fake that accepted what the real store does not (`CLAUDE.md` rule 15). Step 3's "built" was true only against that fake.

Decision. `EventFilter` gains `event_ids`, a filter on the event's own id, compiled into the adapter's `WHERE` clause like `edge_ids`, and extraction uses it. The stand-in now resolves `value_filters` as the adapter does (the five top-level names, otherwise `properties`) and honours `event_ids`. Tests that would fail, each shown red first: the conformance case `test_event_filter_event_ids_restricts_to_those_events` (red: both emails on the link returned), and, with the corrected stand-in, five cases in `test_email_extraction.py` against the old lookup. **Not seen:** an extraction on the live Enron case; the default model is very small, so what it finds may be thin.

## ADR-092 — The emails behind a link go onto the canvas as Documents, and a Document opens full screen to read

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as four multiple-choice questions after the owner said "I need the events to show up as documents on the canvas" and "when I double click document based events, I need full screen display of the text"). It changes ADR-089 decision 2 (the emails were listed in the Inspector only) and narrows the ADR-089 choice the owner made then (no Document node for an email nobody has extracted from).

Decision.

1. **Show emails puts the emails on the canvas.** Choosing *Show emails (n)* on a link writes each email on that link **inside the timeline's brushed window** (every email on the link when nothing is brushed) into the graph as a `Document`, linked to the sender and the recipient by `MENTIONED_IN`, the shape extraction already writes (ADR-089 step 3), and adds them to the canvas. Ids are derived from the event, so showing the same emails again writes nothing new. They are kept, audited, and seen by anyone who can see the case, under each email's own handling.
2. **Never a silent cut (rule 2).** If the emails would take the working set past its cap, nothing is written and the answer is the typed `limit_exceeded` with its three options; the check runs before the graph write, so a refused request leaves nothing behind. The analyst narrows the brush and asks again.
3. **Who may.** Writing needs Editor on the case; reading the emails follows the link-events rules (the link must be visible; one refusal for hidden and missing; on a branch, the visible parents' emails on that link, ADR-084 Amendment 2). The Inspector's Emails list stays for a selected link.
4. **Double-click on any Document opens the reader**, an overlay over the whole work area inside the Glass (canvas and panels): its title, and for an email its sender, recipient and date; the full text with the entities already accepted marked in place; *Extract entities* for an email; *Close* or Escape returns to the same view, nothing moved. This holds for every Document with text (emails and documents from the Ingest Studio); double-click no longer expands a Document, which stays in its right-click menu.
5. **Where the reader's text comes from.** A document's stored extraction text where there is one (the Dossier's source); otherwise, for an email, the event it was made from (`event_id`), read through the analytics port with the case's scope rules and its handling filter. A Document the caller cannot see in the case answers as one that does not exist.

Not decided here. Paging the emails onto the canvas in smaller batches; a reader for a document with no text at all (it says so); placing the Documents in a ring around their link rather than by the layout.

Consequences. Built in three commits: (1) the server route that writes the emails in the window as Documents, with the cap checked first; (2) the Glass: *Show emails* sends the brushed window and draws the delta, and the reader route and overlay; (3) double-click on a Document opens the reader, with a keyboard case (rule 13). Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken: the window narrows what is written; showing twice writes nothing new; past the cap nothing is written and the answer is `limit_exceeded`; a Viewer cannot write; a hidden link and a missing one refuse alike and write nothing; the reader refuses a Document the caller cannot see as a missing one; an email's text comes from its event when nothing was extracted; Escape closes the reader and the view is unchanged.

### ADR-092, Amendment 1 (4 October 2026) — only an event with text becomes a Document; which links are email was misread

Context. The owner asked, while step 2 was being built, whether every demo dataset's linked events are picked up, PaySim's transactions included. Each loader ties its events to their graph link by the link's own id (Enron `pair_edge_id`, PaySim `paysim-tx-{id}`, HMP's incidents substituted with the real graph ids), so *Show events* finds them on every dataset; Fixture Corp has no events. But ADR-092 decision 1, as step 1 built it, would have written a PaySim transaction or an HMP incident as a "(no subject)" Document.

Decision.

1. **Only an event that carries text is written as a Document** (an email's `excerpt`). Events on the link without text are counted and said (`without_text`), never dropped silently; a link none of whose events carries text is refused, `422 not_documents`, and nothing is written. In the Glass only a link between email addresses puts its events on the canvas; any other keeps the Inspector list.
2. **Which links are email: `Endpoint.endpoint_kind`.** The Glass decided "emails" from the source node's `properties.kind`, a field nothing carries (the ontology and the Enron loader use `endpoint_kind`), so every Enron link said *Show events* and its count said records. `eventsNoun` now takes the node and reads `endpoint_kind` itself, the one place that decides it; its test uses the node the Enron loader writes, and the earlier test, which passed the string `"email"` and so agreed with the defect, was replaced.

Tests, each shown red first: `test_a_link_whose_events_have_no_text_is_refused_and_writes_nothing`, `test_events_without_text_are_counted_not_written`, `linkEventsApi.test.ts` (red: a real Enron address read as events), and the keyboard case in `link-menu.spec.ts` that *Show emails* sends the brushed window and draws the Documents (red with the call unwired).

Build note (4 October 2026). All three steps of ADR-092 are built: step 1 `0c0e3d4`, step 2 `0e0b597` (with Amendment 1), step 3 in the commit that adds this note: `reader/DocumentReader.tsx` and `reader/readerApi.ts`, an overlay over the work area in `App.tsx`, and in `GlassCanvas.tsx` a double-click or Enter on a Document calls `onOpenDocument` rather than expanding. Tests shown red first: `DocumentReader.test.tsx` (before the component existed) and `keyboard/reader.spec.ts` (the canvas case red with the Document rule turned off); registry `READER_ACTIONS`. **Not seen:** the reader on the live Enron case.

### ADR-084, Amendment 3 (4 October 2026) — the case picker lists each case once, with its branches beneath it

Context. The owner, looking at *Choose a case*, asked why three "Enron corpus (real data, this machine only) · n selected" rows sat in the list beside the case they came from. They were branches made while testing *Branch selected*: each is a case of its own (decision 1), named after its parent. ADR-084 designed the tab strip and the Branches menu but said nothing about the picker, which listed every case flat and ignored `branched_from`. Owner's choice, from three: nested under the parent.

Decision. The picker lists each original case once, in its usual order, followed by every branch in its family, indented, oldest first, each labelled "branch" beside the caller's level. A family is grouped by the rule the tab strip already uses (`branchFamily`: a branch of a branch belongs to the original; if the original is not visible to the caller, the oldest listed ancestor heads the family, decision 4). No case is left out, and every row still opens and removes as before.

Tests, shown red first: `nestCases` in `cases.test.ts` (order, a branch of a branch, an unseen original, nothing dropped) and the picker case in `CasePicker.test.tsx` (red: the branch was listed apart from its case).

### ADR-084, Amendment 4 (14 October 2026) — one tree of cases and branches; a branch deleted from the Glass

Status: accepted 14 October 2026 — the owner: "the current display method for the Branch and main case
is very confusing, i need a method to delete a branch as through the Glass view", and of the options
put to them, "One tree".

Context. Two displays disagreed. The top bar's case menu listed every case and branch flat, each branch
named "Branch of <case> (n nodes)"; the Cases drawer showed tabs, open or hidden, and a "Branches (n
open of m)" list where a branch could be discarded — but never the branch on screen.

Decision.

1. **One tree, in both places.** The case menu and the Cases drawer show the same component
   (`CaseTree`): each original case once, in `nestCases`' order (Amendment 3), its branches indented
   beneath it, oldest first. A branch is named for what it holds and when it was made — "2 nodes · 14
   Oct 16:40" (UTC) — while it keeps the name branching gave it, and by its own name once renamed.
   The case on screen is marked ("you are here").
2. **On a branch, the menu's button says where it sits:** the case it came from, then the branch
   ("Operation Ledger (synthetic demo) › ⑂ 2 nodes · 14 Oct 16:40").
3. **A branch's ⋯ offers Open, Rename and Delete in place.** Rename is its Author's; Delete is its
   Author's or an administrator of the unit's, the same soft remove as any case (ADR-052 Amendment 7:
   it leaves every list for everyone; nothing is deleted from the stores), asked once in the row.
   **Deleting the branch on screen is allowed** and returns to the case it came from. A refusal is
   said in the row and the branch stays.
4. **Tabs go.** Opening, hiding and the open/hidden count leave the Glass; the server's per-account
   `tab_hidden` flag is left unread.
5. **Tests**, each shown red first: `CaseTree.test.tsx` (7; plants red: 5), `cases.test.ts` (+3),
   `CaseSwitcher.test.tsx` (+1); `keyboard/case-tree.spec.ts` with `CASE_TREE_ACTIONS` (open, rename,
   delete, delete the branch on screen).

### ADR-092, Amendment 2 (4 October 2026) — correction: no email could be written as a Document; the ontology now declares what it carries

Seen by the owner on the live Enron case: *Show emails* put nothing on the canvas and *Extract entities* answered "'Document' does not declare properties 'event_id, message_id, sent_at' in its `properties` or `identifiers`". Both write an email as a `Document` with those three properties (ADR-089 step 3, ADR-092 step 1), and the ArcadeDB adapter checks every write against the ontology (`ontology/validation.py`), where `Document` declared only `title`; so every such write was refused, and no email ever became a Document on a real store.

Cause. Every test of those writes used a graph stand-in that kept whatever it was given: the third stand-in this week that accepted what the real dependency refuses (`CLAUDE.md` rule 15, after ADR-089 Amendment 1's lookup and ADR-084 Amendment 2's case filter).

Decision. `Document` declares `sent_at` (datetime), `message_id` (string) and `event_id` (string), all optional; the ontology version stays 11 for the reason ADR-079 gives (nothing a recipe writes, an index or an adapter reads changes for an existing load). An email without a message id is written without the property, never with a null the `string` type refuses. The stand-in now calls the adapter's own `validate_properties` on every node and link, so the two cannot disagree again. Tests: with the corrected stand-in, nine extraction and Show-emails cases failed with the owner's message before the ontology change and pass after; `test_an_email_without_a_message_id_is_written_without_one`. The API must restart to apply the schema (`make refresh`).

## ADR-093 — A selected node is seen: drawn larger with a bold ring, listed in the Inspector, and counted on the canvas

Status: accepted 4 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as two multiple-choice questions after the owner said "the nodes do not get highlighted when I select them" and asked for the selection to be easier to navigate).

Context. Spec 02 §4 gave a selected node a "2px brass stroke, 1px surface gap". The code drew the 2 pixels and no gap, and the `@sigma/node-border` ring is drawn inside the node's disc, on nodes a few pixels across, so in the browser a selected node looked like any other: a screenshot of the keyboard harness with `n0` selected shows no brass at all. Nothing said "selected" anywhere else on screen except the strip's *Branch selected (n)*.

Decision.

1. **A selected node is drawn 1.6 times its size, with a brass ring (24% of its radius) and a surface-coloured gap (8%) inside it**, two border layers of its own (`selectionRing*`, `selectionGap*`), so the picture in the middle stays about its ordinary size; it is always named. Hover and a found path keep the interaction ring. Fill colour is never changed by selection (hue is entity type only).
2. **The Inspector lists the selection** when more than one node is selected: each by name; choosing one centres the canvas on it; each has a remove (×) that takes it out of the selection.
3. **A chip in the canvas corner says "n selected" with *Clear***, shown while anything is selected.

Consequences. Step 1 (this commit): `nodeAttributes.ts`, the two layers and the scale in `GlassCanvas.tsx`, `workingset/store.ts`'s attribute types; spec 02 §4's table. Found while proving it: the effect that redraws nodes whose selection or hover changed chose them by `borderSize`, so once selection had rings of its own a deselected node kept its rings; it now also redraws a node marked `selected`. Tests that would fail, shown red first: `nodeAttributes.test.ts` (the rings and their absence), and `keyboard/selection-look.spec.ts`, which counts brass pixels painted round a node (red at 0 with the ring shrunk to the old faint width, and red at 42 after deselecting before the redraw fix). Steps 2 and 3 follow with keyboard cases (rule 13).

Build note (4 October 2026). ADR-093 steps 2 and 3 are built: `inspector/SelectionList.tsx` in the Inspector's panel, fed by App's list of selected ids; `canvas/SelectionChip.tsx` in the canvas corner; the canvas handle's `centreOn` (pan and focus, selection kept) and `deselect`. Tests shown red first: the two components' unit tests (before they existed) and `keyboard/selection.spec.ts` (the chip case red with Clear unwired). Found on the way: the chip is a status region, so a keyboard case that found its message by `getByRole("status")` alone matched the chip; it now finds the message by its words. That case also showed the empty-expansion message still named a link type by its id in capitals ("linked by ASSOCIATE_OF"), a place ADR-091 should have reached; it now reads "linked by ‘Associate of’", the type's display name in quotes.

### ADR-092, Amendment 3 (5 October 2026) — Read full screen from the Inspector's opened email

Owner's request after the reader was built: the email opened in the Inspector "opens in a messy manner" in the narrow column, so it gains *Read full screen*. The reader reads a Document, and an email opened in the Inspector may not have been written as one yet, so the Inspector hands the reader the email itself (`readerViewOf`: the id it would be written under, `email:<event id>`, its subject, text, date, ends and link); the reader asks for the Document first and shows the handed email if there is none. Extracting from it writes the Document, and the reader reads that from then on. Found while building it: the server's reader named the link's source as the sender whatever the email's direction, where the Inspector's From reads an inbound email as sent by the far end; the reader now follows the direction. Tests shown red first: `LinkEvents.test.tsx` (the hand-over, and no button where nothing can show it), `DocumentReader.test.tsx` (the handed email shown when there is no Document), `test_an_inbound_email_is_from_the_far_end_as_the_inspector_says`, and the keyboard case in `link-events.spec.ts` (red with the button switched off).

## ADR-094 — Content the model can read: any record or entity may carry text, an image or a video, designated in the Ingest Studio, read and extracted from as Enron's emails are

Status: accepted 5 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as six multiple-choice questions over two rounds and answered in chat). It generalises ADR-089 and ADR-092 from Enron's emails to any content, from demo and real datasets alike.

Context. The owner asked for "the email idea" to extend to messages from phones and, in their answer, from "any device that has text, image or video content", and for the Ingest Studio to "allow objects to be designated as documents, images and videos that can be used by the LLM for entity extraction": "when modelling an object data type, the Ingest Studio must have the ability to designate whether the object has content that can be used for entity extraction". What exists: `ModelPort` already has `extract` (text), `transcribe` (audio, Whisper) and `describe_image` (vision, Moondream); the extraction pipeline and review queue exist; the deployment runs an object store (MinIO); spec 09 §7 describes an unstructured path (documents, images, audio and video, each with an extraction profile) that is not built; a structured recipe cannot say a column is content; the demo phone dataset (`demo_fixtures/cdr.py`) holds calls, not messages; ADR-089's email path reads text from an event's `excerpt` and is reached only on an email link.

Decision.

1. **Content comes in two shapes.** *On a link*: a message between two ends (an email, an SMS, a chat message) is an event on their link, as an Enron email is. *Held by an entity*: a photo, video or saved file on a device (or held by an endpoint, person or organisation) belongs to that entity.
2. **The Ingest Studio designates content, in both its screens.** In a structured recipe, when a source's rows are modelled, a column may be marked as content: *message text*, *document text*, or a *file reference* to an image or a video. On an event row the content belongs to the event (shape one); on an entity row it is held by the entity (shape two). The unstructured path of spec 09 §7 (files uploaded or pointed at: documents, images, videos) is built too, each file becoming content held by the entity the analyst names or standing alone. Designation is a declaration in the recipe, validated at save and at run like the rest of it; no expression language (rule 8).
3. **Every content item is a `Document` with a `media_kind`**: `text`, `image` or `video`. One type, so *Show messages*, the canvas, the reader and extraction work for all three; the ontology adds `media_kind` (enum) to `Document`. Files are kept in the deployment's object store, never in the graph; a Document carries a reference to its object.
4. **Held content is linked by a new relationship type, `HOLDS`**: from `Device`, `Endpoint`, `Person` or `Organisation` to `Document`, basis Direct (the source records the holding). This changes the ontology to **version 12**, and every published recipe is flagged once to be re-pinned (spec 09 §4's proactive flagging), as ADR-055 Amendment 1's bump did.
5. **Extraction by kind.** Text: `extract` as today. Image: `describe_image` gives a description and the text it reads (OCR); entities are extracted from that text, and the region of the image is the locator. Video: its audio is `transcribe`d and entities are extracted from the transcript, with the time in the recording as the locator; frames are not analysed. Face matching and biometric identification stay out of scope (spec 09 §7). Every finding is inferred until a person accepts it (rule 5).
6. **Reading.** The full-screen reader (ADR-092) shows text as today, an image with its description and the text read from it, and a video with its player and transcript. *Show emails* becomes *Show messages (n)* (named emails on an email link, messages on any other link whose events carry content), and a node holding content offers *Show content (n)*.
7. **The demo gains synthetic device messages and media** (rule 9: synthetic, in-repo): SMS with text on the phone dataset's links, and a few synthetic images and short videos held by its devices, so every path can be seen without a real dataset. Real datasets reach the same paths through the Studio, only on the owner's machine and under the real-data exceptions (rule 9, ADR-035 §C3).

Build order (owner's choice, each step usable on its own). **Step 1, messages:** the Studio's content marking on event rows, a recipe's message text written to the event and readable, the synthetic SMS, and the email path generalised (*Show messages*, Documents on the canvas, reader, extraction) to any link whose events carry text. **Step 2, media:** the object store, image description and video transcription, the reader's image and video views, the content marking on entity rows, and `HOLDS` (ontology version 12). **Step 3, files:** the unstructured screen of spec 09 §7 (upload or point at files) and synthetic held media in the demo.

Not decided here. Which archive formats are unpacked, and how deep (spec 09 lists one level); thumbnails on the canvas for an image Document; how long a video may be before transcription is refused or queued; whether a Document's file may be downloaded from the reader, and under what handling.

Consequences. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, to be written first in each step: a recipe that marks a column as content writes it so the reader shows it; a recipe that marks a non-text column as message text is refused at save; content on a link a principal cannot see is not readable (one refusal for hidden and missing); an image Document's description and OCR text are what extraction reads; a video's transcript is; a finding is inferred until accepted; a file is never stored in the graph; `HOLDS` refuses an end type it does not declare; the ontology at version 12 flags every recipe pinned to 11.

### ADR-081, Amendment 3 (5 October 2026) — step D built: a recipe may name only a Direct relationship type

Built as ADR-081 decision 3 and Amendment 1 item 7 stated, with no new decision: `services/ingest/recipe_rules.py` refuses a recipe link naming a Probabilistic type, `SAME_AS`, `NOT_SAME_AS` or a type the ontology lacks; Map's save calls it (`422 recipe_rule`, each problem named, and the Glass shows those words rather than a status) and `run_recipe` calls it again after its ontology-version check, before any write. No recipe in the repository names a refused type (the one `SAME_AS` mention is a comment in `seizure_recipe.yaml`). An overlay type promoted as Direct (ADR-090 Amendment 1 item 2) is accepted once ADR-090's overlay is built, since the rule reads the ontology in force. Tests shown red first: `test_recipe_rules.py` (6, red before the module existed; the run refused against a graph that fails on any call), the Map save case (red: 200), and `rowTemplateSave.test.ts` (red: the bare status).

Build note (5 October 2026). ADR-094 step 1 (messages) is built: `ContentBinding` and `RecipeEdge.content`; the rule that content needs a time; the engine keeping each row's text on the link's event (through staging) as `excerpt`, `truncated` and `content_kind`, never on the graph link; Map's *Text the model can read* and *Column holding the text*, and the marked column counted as mapped (`MapScreen` now uses `rowTemplate.boundFieldNames` rather than its own copy of it); the synthetic SMS (`demo_fixtures/sms.py`, sharing `B_PARTY` with the CDR fixture), its recipe fixture, and `seed_ingest_folder` writing `carrier-a-sms.csv`; in the Glass, a phone link's events named messages, *Show messages* putting those with text on the canvas, and a link of calls only told as a notice; a message Document titled by its first words. Tests shown red first: `test_message_content.py` (5, run against a throwaway object store on loopback, since every recipe run stages through it), the SMS seed case, the title case, `linkEventsApi`, `linkLabel`, `emailDocuments`, `rowTemplate` and `ElementInspector.content` unit cases. **Not covered:** the Ingest Studio has no keyboard registry at all (a gap older than this step); the new controls are native selects.

### ADR-094, Amendment 1 (5 October 2026) — ontology version 12, and a Studio run stores its events

Two things recorded as step 2 began. **Version 12** is in force (decisions 3 and 4): `Document` gains `media_kind` (text, image, video) and `object_ref`; `HOLDS` runs from `Device`, `Endpoint`, `Person` or `Organisation` to `Document`, Direct. Every recipe fixture in the repository (23) is moved from 11 to 12 with it; a recipe published in a running deployment is flagged by `flag_stale` when the API starts, and is reopened and published again from the Studio, one at a time (there is no single command for all of them). The current version is pinned in one test, `test_content_ontology.py`; `test_paysim_ontology.py` no longer pins it. **A defect found on the way, older than this record:** `run_published_recipe` dropped the events a run produced, so no recipe run from the Studio ever reached the analytics store (only the seed scripts called `load_events`), and the timeline, *Show messages* and extraction found nothing for Studio-loaded data. A run now stores them once the graph write commits. Tests shown red first: `test_content_ontology.py` (7) and `test_studio_run_events.py` (red: 0 of 12 events stored).

Build note (5 October 2026). ADR-094 step 2 (media) is built. Server (`14ee9fa`): the `MediaStore` port with its conformance suite written first (in-memory and object-store adapters; a planted off-name file must be refused, since a missing name passes by default deny), `adapters/media_objectstore`, held content on entity rows (`document_text`, `image_file`, `video_file`) through resolution, staging and the load, `HOLDS` from each holder to one `Document` per file, `DocumentContentService` (file, extraction by kind, acceptance) and three routes, the reader reporting `media_kind` and `has_file` and reading held text. Glass (this commit): the reader's picture and player, fetched with the analyst's token, and extraction and acceptance through the Document routes for held content; Map's *Content this holds* on an entity, its column counted as mapped. Tests shown red first: `test_held_content.py` (11), `test_document_content.py` (8), the reader's media cases (server 2, Glass 3), the Map entity case, the media store suite. **Not seen:** the vision and transcription models on real files; whether the speech service accepts a video container as audio is assumed from its documentation, not tried.

Build note (5 October 2026). ADR-094 step 3 (files) is built: `DocumentContentService.upload` and `POST /v1/investigations/{id}/documents` (Editor; a marking the uploader could read and a legal basis required; a holder `HOLDS` allows and can see; the cap checked first; the upload's name check now takes the content kinds, since the studio's source list lacked `.mov`, `.webm`, `.webp` and `.gif`); the Glass's `AddFiles`, reached from the studio's new **Files** stage, from *Add files* under the canvas strip and from a holder's menu; the synthetic phone extraction and its recipe fixture. Tests shown red first: the upload service (6), the route (11), `AddFiles` (3), the studio's Files stage (2), and `keyboard/add-files.spec.ts` (registry `ADD_FILES_ACTIONS`; the menu case red with its entry switched off). **Not built:** spec 09 §7's extraction profile, and document formats other than plain text (PDF, DOCX, RTF, EML), which need a text reader; both are recorded in spec 09.

## ADR-095 — Extraction uses a real extraction model, reads a whole email, decoded; the Inspector's email list puts emails on the canvas

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (owner's choices, put as three multiple-choice questions after testing the Enron case: the messages did not go onto the canvas, the reader stopped at 4,000 characters, and *Extract entities* found nothing in an email naming a company executive, a city and the Board of Directors; and the owner's ruling, the same day: "while Enron dataset is for this machine only the features that we discussed should be available across the whole product"). ADR-089 and ADR-092 are unchanged except where this says so.

Context. Four causes, each seen on the owner's deployment, not assumed.

1. **Live extraction ran on the conformance model.** `services/api/app.py` passed `CONFORMANCE_MODEL` (`qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct`) to the email and document extraction services, against `adapters/model_litellm`'s own rule ("this name is conformance-only, never hardcoded into a caller outside `tests/conformance`") and spec 03 §5.2's default (a 7–14B model). Re-run on the owner's email, it returned a person's name the model ran together, with a birth date and an alias of its own, four sentences of its own as `Endpoint`s, and a city; every item was rightly dropped (confidences on a 0–10 scale read as hundredths, and values not in the text). ADR-020 already says this model is "a poor extractor in absolute terms".
2. **An Enron body was never decoded.** `demo_fixtures/enron.py` read each body with `get_payload(decode=False)`, so quoted-printable stayed encoded: `=20` and soft line breaks (a name broken by `=` and a line break) split the very words extraction must find verbatim.
3. **The excerpt was cut at 4,000 characters** (ADR-089 Amendment 1), so the reader and extraction both saw only the start of a long email.
4. **The Inspector's Emails list could not put emails on the canvas** (ADR-092 decision 3 kept the list as a list); the owner opened the emails there, and no Document was written.

Decision.

1. **A deployment's extraction model is its own, chosen by the system administrator on the setup harness's Models screen** (the owner's ruling, the same day: "the LLM selection should be available in the admin harness so that system admin can configure it, use the model that I selected as the default one the product ships with"), written to `osprey.yaml` as `models.extraction`, and never the conformance model. The choice is from a closed list of supported local models, because each must be pinned (ADR-020) before a deployment may pull it; a name off the list is refused by the config's own validation. The list, read from the registry's manifests and checked by the same method against the 0.5B pin:

   | Model | Licence | Download | Manifest digest | |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `qwen2.5:7b-instruct` | Apache-2.0 | 4.68 GB | `845dbda0ea48ed749caafd9e6037047aa19acfcfd82e704d7ca97d631a0b697e` | **the default the product ships with** |
   | `qwen2.5:14b-instruct` | Apache-2.0 | 8.99 GB | `7cdf5a0187d5c58cc5d369b255592f7841d1c4696d45a8c8a9489440385b22f6` | |

   The Conduit's email and document extraction use it; the conformance suite keeps `qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct`. It is pulled and digest-verified by the same script as the others, and the deployment reports healthy only once it is present. Adding a model to the list is adding a row here and its pin.
2. **The model is given room for a whole email, and nothing is cut silently (rule 2).** The extraction model is served with a 32,768-token context. Text longer than one extraction window is read in overlapping windows and the findings joined, each located in the whole text; nothing past a window is dropped unread.
3. **An email is kept whole and decoded.** The Enron loader decodes each body (quoted-printable, base64, the declared character set) and keeps all of it on the event; the reader shows it all and extraction reads it all. `excerpt` keeps its name and now holds the whole body; `truncated` is always false for a new load. The owner reloads the case's events (`--replace-events`).
4. **The Inspector's Emails list has *Put on the canvas***, doing exactly what *Show emails (n)* does from the link menu (ADR-092 decisions 1 and 2: the emails inside the timeline's window, written as Documents, or `limit_exceeded`). Keyboard-reachable (rule 13).
5. **None of this is Enron's alone (the owner's ruling).** Enron is a dataset admitted for this machine only (ADR-053); what it showed is built for every source the product reads:
   - *Decoding*: one shared reader of a message body (`conduit_common/message_text.py`: transfer encoding, character set, the plain-text part of a multipart message) that the Enron loader uses and any email source after it must use; it is not a demo fixture's private code.
   - *Whole text*: the Ingest Studio keeps a recipe's text column whole on its events (phone messages and any other text a recipe marks, ADR-094), and content an entity holds is kept whole; no 4,000-character cut remains on any path that writes text for reading or extraction.
   - *The models*: every model the Conduit uses for analysts' work is the deployment's own, chosen on the Models screen and named in `osprey.yaml`: `models.extraction` (decision 1), `models.vision`, `models.transcription` and `models.embedding`, whose lists hold today's models only (`moondream:1.8b-v2-q4_K_M`, `Systran/faster-whisper-tiny.en`, `all-minilm:22m-l6-v2-fp16`) until the owner chooses others; no production caller names a conformance model. Extraction from a held document, image or video uses the same windows (decision 2).
   - *The canvas*: *Put on the canvas* serves every link whose events carry text, phone messages as well as emails.

Consequences. The deployment downloads 4.68 GB once, and extraction is slower per email than on the 0.5B model. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken, each to be shown red first: the Conduit's extraction services are built with the configured models and never a conformance one, checked by a scan of `services/` for a conformance name outside the conformance suite; a Studio recipe's text over 4,000 characters is kept whole on its event; the rendered pull script and LiteLLM config carry the extraction model and its digest, and its context size; a text longer than one window is read in more than one call and a finding from the second window is kept with its locator in the whole text; a quoted-printable Enron body is decoded, and a body over 4,000 characters is kept whole; *Put on the canvas* in the Inspector writes the emails as the menu does, by keyboard.

## ADR-096 — The side panels fold away: an accordion each for the Inspector, the Query builder and Metrics, a preview open, denser type

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (owner, in chat, three messages: "the inspect panel very cluttered with all sorts of options, can you tidy this up and put all options as collapsible menu under accordians"; "Don't put everything into a single accordian, create separate accordians for Inpector, Query Builder and Metrics, only have preview there as default view"; "reduce the font sizes and spacing to make it easy to view and naviate"). The details below are mine, within those asks, and recorded so they can be overruled.

Context. A selected link showed five parts stacked, all open: its details, *Change this link…*, Notes, Emails (with *Put on the canvas*, ADR-095) and Change history. A selected node showed four tabs: Properties, Provenance, Source and Judgements.

Decision.

0. **Each of the three side panels has its own accordion** (ADR-085's column keeps the three panels apart, each movable and sized as before); the parts of one panel fold within it, never into another's. Each opens on its preview, the part read at a glance, and every other part starts folded: the Inspector's *Details* or *Properties* (below), the Query builder's *Pattern* (its nodes, *Preview*, *Run* and what they answer; *Add a pattern variable*, *Connect two pattern nodes*, *Save this pattern* and *Load a saved pattern* fold), and Metrics' *Ranking* (*Communities* and *Filter* fold; more than one may now be open at once).
6. **The style: minimalist and bordered** (the owner's choice, kept when a design review proposed borderless rows; the review's other points taken): one hairline box per part (`--border-subtle`, `--r-control`) with `--sp-4` between, the header a full-width row at `--fs-12` 600 with a chevron on the left that turns when open (no turn under `prefers-reduced-motion`), `--surface-hover` on hover and focus.
5. **Denser type and spacing in the three panels**: the panel title at `--fs-13`, the body and its controls at `--fs-12` with `--lh-12`, and the body's padding and gaps at `--sp-8` and `--sp-4`, from the tokens only; the rest of the Glass is unchanged.
1. **Every part of the Inspector is a section with a header that opens and closes it** (a button with `aria-expanded`, its content a labelled region). A link's sections: *Details*, *Change this link*, *Notes*, the link's events (*Emails (n)*, *Messages (n)* or *Events (n)*) and *Change history*. A node's: *Properties*, *Provenance*, *Source* and *Judgements*, replacing the tabs.
2. **What starts open:** a link's *Details*, a node's *Properties*, and with no node selected *Judgements*; every other section starts closed.
3. **The menus still reach their part.** *Change link…*, *Add a note*, *Show emails (n)* and *Show change history* open their section as well as doing what they did (ADR-080, ADR-075, ADR-089).
4. **A closed section keeps what is in it.** Its content stays in the page, hidden, so a half-written note or change is not lost by closing it, and nothing is fetched again on opening it. Which sections are open lasts for the selection, not across a reload.

Consequences. Spec 02 §2. ADR-070's Metrics strip (closed, one at a time) is replaced; its keyboard id `ranking-section-opens-by-keyboard-and-loads-the-list` becomes `ranking-opens-loaded-and-folds-by-keyboard`, and the Query builder gains `open-a-folded-part-by-keyboard`. Tests that would fail if an invariant were broken: each panel opening on its preview with the rest folded (`QueryBuilderPanel.test.tsx`, `MetricsPanel.test.tsx`); a link's sections, which start open and closed, opening and closing by keyboard; a menu hand-over opening its section; a node's sections replacing the tabs, Judgements open with no node; a half-written note surviving its section's closing (`inspector/Inspector.test.tsx`, `keyboard/inspector.spec.ts`, registry `INSPECTOR_ACTIONS`).

## ADR-097 — The design review of 6 October 2026 adopted, against DESIGN.md v0.2, in three steps

Status: accepted 6 October 2026 (owner: a usability review of the Glass by Claude Design, sixteen items in priority order, and `spec/design/DESIGN.md` v0.2 placed in the repository; the owner's answer to the five conflicts put to them: "go with your suggestions"). ADR-084, ADR-085, ADR-086 and ADR-096 are unchanged except where this says so.

**DESIGN.md and tokens.css.** `spec/design/DESIGN.md` is the design contract: a value on screen that it does not hold is drift. `apps/workspace/src/design/tokens.css` stays the binding implementation (`CLAUDE.md`), and the two agree, checked: every colour in `tokens.css` is in `DESIGN.md` (its one extra, `#313334`, is named in passing with no role), and the radii match in value under other names (`--r-0` `--r-canvas`, `--r-1` `--r-control`, `--r-2` `--r-panel`, `--r-3` `--r-overlay`, `--r-pill` `--r-chip`). A change to either is made to both. The review asked for `npx impeccable detect`, which is not installed; its place is taken by `tools/colour_drift_check.py`: every colour literal in the Glass's source is one `DESIGN.md` holds, or the file is a declared mirror of the tokens for the WebGL canvas (`color/tokens.ts`, `color/palette.ts`), or it is named in an allowlist with its reason until fixed.

**The five conflicts, decided (the owner, taking my suggestions).**

1. *Right panel (review item 1).* The three panels of ADR-085 stay stacked, movable and sized, each with its ADR-096 accordion; the column becomes the review's right panel (360px by default, resizable as now), with the review's header rows. Not tabs: tabs would hide two of the three.
2. *Reordering (item 8).* *Move up* and *Move down* leave the grip row for a menu on the panel's header, and Alt+↑ and Alt+↓ on a focused header move the panel; dragging stays. The arrows go.
3. *Accordion style (item 14).* The owner's bordered style stays (ADR-096 decision 6) with the review's hairline weight, chevron on the left and `--fs-12` 600 headers.
