## ADR-120 — The Prison Intelligence Dataset: NIEM pack version 3, per-type link weights, pack-version pinning, and the synthetic case — ACCEPTED (design)

Status: **ACCEPTED by the owner, 23 October 2026** ("Accept ADR-120? Yes"). Rulings taken from the
owner in chat the same day, from options put to him, are quoted at each decision.
Decisions D1 to D9 carry the build brief's own numbers (`01_DOMAIN_MODEL_AND_GENERATOR_BRIEF.md`
§4); D10 is added by the owner's ruling.

**Context.** A demonstration to prison intelligence analysts needs one synthetic case that carries
a prison network and a throw-over investigation end to end (the approved script "Prison
Intelligence Demo: Script v1"). The repository's existing synthetic prison fixture is left exactly
as it is; this is a separate case, the **Prison Intelligence Dataset (PID)**, and no name,
identifier, reference or text of the older fixture is reused. Reading the tree for this record
found six places where the code does not do what the spec or an earlier record says, and they shape
the decisions below:

- A pack bump flags no recipe. `pack_version` is read by no code; `flag_stale`
  (`services/api/studio_recipes.py`) and `StaleRecipeError` (`services/ingest/engine.py`) compare
  only the core `ontology_version`, and the composed ontology discards each pack's name and version
  (`packages/ontology/packs.py`, `compose_with_packs`). ADR-117's Cost recorded this; ADR-108 and
  `packs.py`'s docstring still promise otherwise.
- "A pack only ever adds" is checked by nothing: no code compares pack version N with N+1, and a
  pack's entries skip the JSON Schema the core file is validated against, so a pack edge without
  `basis` loads with `None` and a pack icon is not checked against ADR-079's list.
- The §6.1 weight formula is not monotone in occurrences, and its calibration is a placeholder.
  Measured with `weight.py`'s own arithmetic: a pair whose two ends contact only each other weighs
  2.6192 (raw) at one occurrence and 2.6143 at two in a corpus of 1,000 other occurrences, and the
  same step falls for every such pair once the rest of the corpus holds 57 or more occurrences; its
  raw PMI also swamps the occurrence term (about 4.7 raw for an exclusive pair against 1.2 for a
  hub-to-leaf link). `midpoint` and `scale` are uncalibrated (`weight.py`'s docstring), and the
  parameter set §6.1 requires to be recorded with stored components is not recorded.
- No extraction or Questions path can create a link of a pack type: model extraction proposes
  entities only (`services/extract/profile.py`), edge candidates are deferred
  (`services/extract/writer.py`), and both accept paths write only `MENTIONED_IN`.
- Nothing in the Glass or the Conduit filters by a property of a linked node, and `PatternQuery`
  has no property predicate and, deliberately, no negation (§8.1).
- An entity's picture (ADR-105) is returned by a generic expand: "With all links" draws the
  `DEPICTS` link and the picture `Document` and counts them in its "N links"
  (`explore/ExplorePanel.tsx`; no filter in `graph_arcadedb/access_filter.py`). A *removed* picture
  (`DEPICTS` with `shown: false`) is returned and counted too, because only
  `services/api/entity_pictures.py` reads `shown`. That second point is a defect of ADR-105's build,
  recorded here and not fixed by this record.

**Decisions.**

1. **D1 — The new types go into NIEM pack version 3, additions only** (the owner: "NIEM pack
   version 3"). The precedent is ADR-117; a Studio pipeline chooses the core plus one pack
   (`09_INGEST_STUDIO.md` §1.1) and the custody links already live in NIEM. The core stays at
   version 16. Added:
   - Entity `Establishment`: `pole_class: organisation`, channel `azure`, shape `diamond` (azure
     already carries Organisation's square and FIBO `Account`'s hexagon; no type in the core or any
     pack uses azure with a diamond), icon `building`, identifier `establishment_ref`; properties
     `name` (string, required, indexed), `establishment_ref` (string, required, indexed), `niu_area`
     (string, indexed), `soct_region` (string, indexed), `security_category` (string).
   - Links, each with a label, all `basis: direct` except the last: `HELD_AT` Person →
     Establishment ("held at"; directed, temporal, colour azure); `PART_OF` Location → Location or
     Establishment ("part of"; directed, colour moss); `ADJOINS` Location — Location ("adjoins";
     undirected, colour cyan); `USED_BY` Location → Location ("used by"; directed, colour moss);
     `OCCURRED_AT` Incident → Location ("occurred at"; directed, temporal, colour jade);
     `PASSES_ITEMS_TO` Person → Person ("passes items to"; directed, temporal,
     **`basis: probabilistic`**, colour indigo, property `channel`: string). `PART_OF` and
     `USED_BY` share moss as the two quiet structural place links; their labels tell them apart.
   - Core `DEPICTS` is widened (`extends: true`) to end at `Establishment`, so an establishment can
     carry its own picture (D9); today `entity_pictures.py` refuses one.
   Everything else the case uses is already in the core or in NIEM version 2. Wings, landings,
   cells, yards, visits halls and outside places are core `Location`s; the prison itself is an
   `Establishment`. A person holds an account or a phone through core `USES` (Person → Endpoint);
   core `HOLDS` ends only at `Document`.

2. **D2 — The throw-over event, and "additions only" as a tested property.** `Incident.category`
   gains `throw_over`, and `OCCURRED_AT` (D1) places an incident. The loader accepts a changed enum
   list because it compares nothing between versions; so the guarantee that version 3 is a strict
   superset of version 2 (every version-2 entity type, property, enum value, edge type and edge end
   present and unchanged) is a test that freezes version 2's content and compares, shown red first
   against a planted removal of the kind a real edit makes (dropping an enum value; dropping an
   edge end). A general version-compatibility check in the loader would be its own decision.

3. **D3 — Link weights: one formula, the count normalised per link type, recorded with every
   weight** (the owner: "Amend to normalised PMI"; "Normalise the count per type", which replaces
   his earlier "per-type midpoint/scale"; "Truly fixed weight"; "Same pair, rest held fixed").
   - **The formula** (`01_DOMAIN_MODEL.md` §6.1, amended):
     `weight(e) = normalise( α·log1p(occurrences)/log1p(heavy_type) + β·recency(interval.to) +
     γ·npmi(u,v) )`, with one deployment-wide `midpoint` and `scale`. Dividing the count term by
     the type's own heavy count gives every type the same count term at its heavy count, while
     recency and the mutual-information term weigh the same for every type; the earlier per-type
     midpoint and scale divided those two terms by a different amount per type and did not.
   - **The mutual-information term is normalised PMI**: `npmi(u,v) = pmi(u,v) / −ln p(u,v)`,
     clamped to [−1, 1] (a self-loop is counted twice in a degree, so `p(u)·p(v)` can exceed one);
     1 when `p(u,v) = 1`; 0 wherever `weight.py` returns 0 today (corpus total, pair count or either
     degree zero). α, β, γ and the half-life are unchanged.
   - **Calibration is derived, never hand-tuned.** `midpoint` and `scale` are solved so that, at
     recency 1 and npmi 0, a count term of 0 normalises to the logistic of −1 (≈ 0.27) and a count
     term of 1, the type's heavy count, to the logistic of 2 (≈ 0.88): with the stated α and β,
     `scale` = 1/6 and `midpoint` = 0.2 + 1/6. At npmi 0, one occurrence then draws at about 0.39
     for a type heavy at 40 and about 0.71 for one heavy at 2. npmi 0 flatters those figures: the
     mutual-information term spans 0.6 raw, more than the count term's 0.5, and moves every link's
     logit by up to ±1.8, and in a sparse corpus most pairs score high (one report mention in a
     corpus of 500 with both degrees 3 has npmi of about 0.65). So one-off links in a case like the
     PID draw at about 0.65 to 0.85, the upper half of the six widths; within a type the count still
     orders a pair, and the principal-star test below is checked by arithmetic before it is built.
   - **A structural rule is a fixed weight**: the type's weight is its declared strength, whatever
     its occurrences, recency or mutual information, an exception to the formula that this record
     makes and §6.1 states. The components are still stored.
   - **The invariant, stated exactly:** adding occurrences to one pair, with the rest of the corpus
     and the pair's recency unchanged, never lowers its weight. It does not hold across different
     pairs (a fresh, exclusive link can rightly draw heavier than an old, busy one). On a grid of
     967 series of 300 occurrence counts per heavy count (289,133 steps; each end's other
     occurrences 0 to 10,000, the rest of the corpus 1 to 10 million, heavy 2 to 200), the ruled
     formula gave no decreasing step and raw PMI with the old count term gave 5. The grid never
     reaches `p(u,v) = 1` or a self-loop, so the clamp and the `p(u,v) = 1` rule rest on the
     property test, which covers both; the grid is evidence and the test is the guard.
   - **The rules live in a weights file, `packages/ontology/weights/default.yaml`, beside the
     handling scheme, not in the ontology.** The weights are calibration, not schema: declaring them
     on edge types in `default.yaml` would bump the core and flag every recipe for a change no recipe
     can observe, and a pack's unknown keys are silently dropped today. The shipped file is the one
     every deployment reads; a deployment's own replacement file is not built. It holds an
     append-only list of versions (an old version is never edited, as an ADR is not, which a
     frozen-history test enforces); each version holds α, β, γ, `half_life_days`, `midpoint`,
     `scale`, a `default` rule, and one rule per type.
   - **A rule declares what one occurrence is and what heavy is.** `unit` names the occurrence in
     words and `heavy` the count that is heavy for the type, counted over the data loaded (time is
     carried by the recency term, so the brief's "in 90 days" and "in the window" are not separate
     windows). `occurrences` is set by whoever writes the link (`EdgeWrite.occurrences`, summed on a
     same-pair upsert), so the writer honours the unit: a cell-share source emits one row per pair
     per week shared, which the PID's plan test asserts.
   - **The PID's rules** (the brief's table): `SHARED_CELL_WITH` one week shared, heavy 12; `VISITED`
     one visit (a video visit counts as one), heavy 8; `COMMUNICATED_WITH` one call, heavy 40;
     `TRANSACTED` one transfer (the amount is not in the weight), heavy 6; `MENTIONED_IN` one report,
     heavy 3; `ROLE_IN` one incident, heavy 3; `IN_CONFLICT_WITH` one episode, heavy 2;
     `CO_DEFENDANT_OF`, `FAMILY_OF`, `MEMBER_OF` and `HELD_AT` structural at 0.75, so a standing
     relationship draws in the upper widths beside heavy counted links rather than below a single
     mention; `DEPICTS` structural at 0.2, so a picture link draws thin (under the default rule it
     is exclusive at both ends, npmi 1, and would draw at 0.84, as heavy as the principal's calls to
     the coordinator). Every other type takes the `default` rule: one occurrence, heavy 10.
   - **The parameter set is recorded with every stored weight.** `WeightComponents` gains
     `parameter_set: str | None`, `"<weights version>/<rule>"`, where the rule is the link type's
     own or `default` for a type with none, naming the exact version and rule in the append-only
     file, so every value is recoverable. `None` means the uncalibrated curve that preceded this
     record. A recalibration is a new version, so two weights computed
     under different calibrations are never compared unknowingly.
   - **Existing stored weights are not recomputed by this record.** Edges written before it keep
     their old weight and carry no `parameter_set`, which makes the mix visible. A recompute is
     arithmetic over the stored components, but `GraphPort` has no in-place edge update (a same-pair
     upsert adds occurrences; `supersede_edge` mints a new id), so it is its own record. A deployment
     installed or reseeded after this lands has only current weights.
   - **There is no browser weight function to keep equal.** The Glass draws the stored `weight` it
     is sent (`canvas/nodeAttributes.ts`) and recomputes none; the brief's "browser and server produce
     the same weights" is met as "the weight on the wire is the weight the server computed". This
     reading was set out in the stage 0 plan the owner read; it was not separately ruled. §6.2's
     parity requirement remains the Clique Metric's.

4. **D4 — Prisoner numbers are `Z####ZZ`, synthetic by construction** (the owner: "Z####ZZ";
   "By construction plus test"). A letter, four digits, two letters, as a real prison number is
   shaped, fixed to a leading `Z` and a trailing `ZZ`. The project's sources hold no reserved
   prisoner-number range, so that this sits outside issued ranges rests on this ruling, not on a
   source. `Provenance` has no `synthetic` field and gains none; synthetic identity is proved by
   construction, as the existing fixtures do: prisoner numbers `Z####ZZ`; visitors' National
   Insurance numbers prefixed `QQ`, which is never issued; phones in Ofcom's drama ranges (D5); bank
   accounts `SYN-nnnnn` at "Fictional Bank"; private-cash accounts `PC-<prison number>`; prisoner PIN
   accounts as `Endpoint` `handle` `PIN-<prison number>`; IMEIs with a valid Luhn check digit and
   the test-device TAC prefix `00` (the `imei` adapter checks the Luhn digit only, so the plan test
   checks the prefix).

5. **D5 — Phones use only the drama ranges ADR-103 accepts, and collide with no other fixture.**
   The `msisdn` adapter accepts mobile 07700 900; geographic 0113–0118, 0121, 0131, 0141, 0151 and
   0161 496 0; 020 7946 0; 0191 498 0; 028 9649 6; 029 2018 0; 01632 960; freephone 0808 157 0;
   premium 0909 879 0; UK-wide 0306 999 0; each a block of 1,000. The mobile block is already used
   by other fixtures seeded into the same standard demo, so the PID's outside mobiles come only from
   07700 900600 to 900899 and its other outside numbers from the geographic blocks, about 1,500 in
   all; no real range is used. Some fixtures compute their numbers rather than writing them out
   (the scenario cohorts offset theirs by a checksum of the run name), so the collision test runs
   every other fixture's and seed's own generator, not a text search, and the sub-range moves if it
   collides. National and `+44` forms normalise to the same E.164 value, so the
   script's national-form search problem (J2) is in search, not in the adapter.

6. **D6 — Two datasets, one generator with two size profiles.** `prison-intelligence`
   ("Prison Intelligence Dataset (synthetic)"; source `pid-generator`; case "Prison Intelligence
   Dataset (synthetic demo)"): three establishments, about 1,000 prisoners, 10,000 to 15,000
   links, about 1,000,000 PIN call rows over about 1,500 distinct outside numbers.
   `prison-intelligence-scale` ("Prison Intelligence Dataset: scale cohort (synthetic)"; source
   `pid-scale-generator`; case "Prison Intelligence Dataset: scale cohort (synthetic demo)"): six
   establishments, 3,000 prisoners, 30,000 links (the owner: "3,000 / 30,000"), no call file of its
   own and no pictures. Both are registered in `packages/demo_fixtures/datasets.py` (ADR-099
   Amendment 6 refuses a write naming an unregistered dataset); `SeedDataset` holds id, name, source
   and case name only, so distribution class and delivery belong to the demo-pack manifest (Brief 2).
   **Both, the full call file included, are part of the standard product demo** (the owner: "I
   would include the optional parts into the Standard demo as well"). The establishment is **Fenwick
   Moor Prison** (the owner's choice over the brief's working name), held in one constant; its local
   originator and owning unit are `fenwick-moor-security`, the regional ones `regional-intel-unit`.
   The generated files are produced on demand and never committed (rule 9: the generator and its
   tests are in the repository, its output is not).

7. **D7 — The area scope (J4) does not exist, and this record builds none.** Search takes no
   property filter (`services/api/search.py`), the legend toggles link types only, `PatternQuery`
   has no property predicate, and the map boundary filters working-set nodes by position. Search
   does match every indexed string property of a node (`graph_arcadedb/builders.py`), so typing an
   NIU area finds an `Establishment` carrying it; that is matching, not a filter. The smallest
   change is put to the owner as **ADR-121**. The script's absence query (chapter 11) stays
   unsupported: §8.1 declines negation on purpose.

8. **D8 — `PASSES_ITEMS_TO` is seeded as inferred, the PID's one inferred item at load** (the owner:
   "Seed it as inferred"). No extraction path can propose a link today, so the chapter-6 relay links
   are written by the PID's seed through `GraphPort` with provenance state `inferred`, `extracted_by`
   `"synthetic:pid-extraction-run"` and an `extraction_confidence`, never `asserted`. Rule 5 holds:
   they stay inferred until a person confirms them. The smallest fix that would let a model propose
   them, not built here: model extraction's output schema gains a list of links restricted to the
   ontology's Probabilistic types whose two ends are among the entities proposed or already in the
   document's case, each accepted through the existing review queue and written `inferred`; it is its
   own record. The Glass draws an inferred link dashed whatever its basis (`edgeProgramFor`);
   ADR-081 decision 4's "probabilistic is always dotted" is not what the code does for an inferred
   link, recorded here and not changed. There is no general route to confirm a link (only alert
   triage reaches `confirm_edge`), so the demo points at these links and confirms none. A recipe
   cannot write the type: `recipe_rules.py` refuses a Probabilistic type at save and at run.

9. **D9 — Pictures through the existing `DEPICTS` path** (the owner: "Split B1 data / B3 Glass";
   "Illustrated avatars"). In the demo case each person, establishment, wing, yard, seized handset and
   organised-crime group gets its own picture as an image `Document` linked by `DEPICTS` (ADR-105;
   for an establishment, through D1's widening). People get flat, illustrated avatars built from
   shapes and colours, never photographic and never from an image model; places, handsets and
   groups get drawings or emblems; hotspot yards look like the other yards. Every picture is a PNG
   (one of the four formats `entity_pictures.py` accepts; SVG is refused) of 256 by 256 pixels and
   under 50 KB, drawn by the generator itself, deterministic from the one seed, written with the
   standard library only (no dependency, no licence). **The principal's 49 links include his picture
   link**, because "With all links" returns and counts it; the plan's link constant is set to match.
   An icon chosen by a property value is a Glass change and its own record (Brief 3).

10. **D10 — A recipe pins the version of every pack it names, and a pack bump flags it** (the
    owner: "Build pack-version pinning"; this makes ADR-108's promise true).
    - The composed ontology keeps each pack's name and `pack_version` (`OntologySchema.packs`, a
      map from name to version); a pack file without an integer `pack_version` is refused at load.
    - `Recipe` (and so the committed YAML) and the `studio_recipes` row gain `pack_versions`: a map
      from every pack the recipe's pipeline names in a domain-model node to the version it was
      published against, stamped at publish beside `ontology_version`. The column is `JSONB`, added
      with `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, the table's own precedent. On `Recipe` the field defaults to
      `None`, meaning "not pinned", which is distinct from an empty map, meaning "pinned, names no
      pack".
    - **A recipe published before this record is backfilled, not flagged blind.** At bootstrap,
      every published row with no `pack_versions` whose recipe (read from its committed YAML) names a
      pack is stamped with that pack's last version before this record: NIEM 2, FIBO 1, STIX 1. No
      pack version had ever changed except NIEM's (1 to 2, ADR-117), so this is exact for FIBO and
      STIX, and for NIEM it is never lower than the true one, so it never hides a bump. The backfill
      runs in the same bootstrap, before `flag_stale`; a row whose committed YAML cannot be read is
      flagged, since what it names cannot be known. The NIEM bump to 3 then flags exactly the
      recipes naming NIEM, and no FIBO or STIX recipe; the core's own legacy rule (a null
      `ontology_version` is never flagged) is unchanged.
    - `flag_stale(current_ontology_version, current_pack_versions)` flags a published recipe whose
      core version differs (as today) or any of whose pinned pack versions differs from the loaded
      pack's, in one statement over the `JSONB` column.
    - At run time a flagged Studio recipe is refused first by `RecipeNotRunnableError`
      (`services/api/studio_publish.py`), as today; the engine's `StaleRecipeError` additionally
      refuses a recipe whose pinned pack version differs from the loaded one, whose pinned pack the
      ontology it is handed does not carry, or which names a pack and is not pinned
      (`pack_versions` `None`): a committed recipe, Brief 2's included, never reaches the store
      without saying which pack version it was written for.
    - In this repository no committed recipe names NIEM, so the bump flags no file in the tree; in a
      deployment it flags every published Studio recipe naming NIEM, and its author republishes it.

**Cost.** A pack bump now forces a republish of every recipe naming that pack, as a core bump
already does. The weights file governs every dataset in a deployment, not only the PID: Enron's
mail, PaySim's and the Ledger's transfers and the call fixtures are weighed by the PID's rules for
`COMMUNICATED_WITH` (heavy 40), `TRANSACTED` (heavy 6) and `MENTIONED_IN` (heavy 3), which count
different units at different volumes there; weighted degree and the strength filter follow. Weights
stored before this record keep the old curve until a recompute exists; the `parameter_set` shows
the mix. Normalised PMI pulls down a "number everyone calls" less than raw PMI did, because the term
is bounded. A structural link's thickness says nothing about recency or exclusivity. The area scope and the absence
query the script asks for are not delivered. The relay links are inferred by a seed, not by a model
run, and say so in their provenance. The principal's picture is a node in his star.

**Revisit if.** A deployment needs a type's weight to depend on a property (a transfer's amount) or
on a window rather than on counts; one dataset's calibration visibly distorts another's in one
deployment (then rules per dataset); the property test finds a decreasing step; a pack needs
pinning at a finer grain than the whole pack.

**Tests that fail if this is violated.** Each new check is shown red against a planted violation of
the shape the code really emits before it is trusted (rule 15).
- **D1, D2:** `tests/ontology/test_niem_pack_v3.py`: every new type with its declared ends, basis,
  temporality and label; channel and shape unique over the core and every pack composed together;
  `Establishment`'s icon in ADR-079's list and every new link's colour one of the nine channels
  (a pack's colours, like its icons, skip the JSON Schema); `DEPICTS` reaching `Establishment`; `throw_over`
  accepted and an unknown category refused; version 3 a superset of a frozen version 2.
- **D10:** `tests/ontology/test_pack_versions.py` (the composed ontology carries each pack's
  version; a pack without one refused); `tests/services/api/test_studio_recipes_store.py` (a pack
  bump flags only recipes pinning that pack; a recipe naming no pack is not flagged; the backfill
  stamps a legacy NIEM recipe at 2 and a legacy FIBO one at 1); `tests/ingest/test_studio_publish_pipeline.py`
  (publish stamps `pack_versions`; a flagged pack recipe is refused by `RecipeNotRunnableError`);
  `tests/ingest/test_recipe_engine_end_to_end.py` (a stale pack pin, a pinned pack the ontology
  lacks, and a recipe naming a pack with no pin are each refused by `StaleRecipeError`; a recipe
  pinning an empty map runs). The backfill: an unreadable committed YAML flags its row.
- **D3:** `tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_weight_rules.py`: the same-pair invariant over a wide
  property-test grid for every rule, including `p(u,v) = 1` and a self-loop; the calibration
  reproduced on a small fixture (at recency 1 and npmi 0, each counted type's heavy count at 0.88
  and one occurrence at the value the formula gives for that type, 0.39 at heavy 40); a structural
  type's weight equal to its strength whatever its occurrences; every stored component carrying the
  current `parameter_set`, which resolves in the weights file (a type with no rule to `default`); no
  earlier version of the weights file edited (a frozen copy compared); the weight on the wire equal
  to the weight computed; on the PID's principal star, the coordinator's call link and the
  shared-payer transfer links among its heaviest and a one-off cell share and the picture link among
  its lightest.
- **D4 to D9:** `tests/scenarios/test_pid_plan.py`, the plan without a store: every constant and
  exact multiset, both profiles, the four gaps absent by construction, no identifier that could be
  real (D4), every number passing `msisdn()` and none used by any other fixture or seed (D5),
  cell-share occurrences equal to weeks shared (D3), `PASSES_ITEMS_TO` written `inferred` and never
  `asserted` (D8), every picture reproducible from the seed, a PNG within the limits above,
  depicting exactly one entity and drawn by the generator with no file read from anywhere else (D9).
  `tests/scenarios/test_pid_files.py` for the files' row counts, and each picture accepted by the
  real picture route's own validation.
  `tests/demo_fixtures/test_datasets.py`: both datasets registered and a write naming either
  accepted (D6). `tests/ingest/test_recipe_rules.py`: a recipe naming `PASSES_ITEMS_TO` refused at
  save and at run (D8). `tests/services/api/test_pid_access_control.py`, against ArcadeDB through
  `GRAPH_PORT_ADAPTERS` as the existing access-control tests are, ignored by `make test` and run by
  the live `conformance` job (the `Makefile` and `ci.yml` entries handed to the owner as a diff,
  since both are protected, and kept in step by `test-file-coverage-check`): the SECRET link invisible to the OFFICIAL analyst in canvas, counts, paths and degrees, and
  the analyst's answer equal to the answer over the case without it; the principal's degree as the
  analyst sees it, the count "With all links" shows, equal to 49 with his picture link among them
  (J1).

### ADR-120, Amendment 1 (23 October 2026) — a recipe pins the packs it names and the packs whose types it writes

Status: **ACCEPTED by the owner, 23 October 2026** ("I accept ADR-120 Amendment 1"). Decision 1 is
his ruling in chat ("Named packs + types written"); decisions 2 to 6 are the coordinator's, accepted
with it. Found by the
adversarial review of stage 2's tests before any of D10's recipe code was written.

1. **A recipe pins every pack it names and every pack whose types it writes.** D10 pinned only the
   packs a pipeline's domain-model nodes name, but a recipe can write a pack's types without naming
   it: `tests/ingest/test_pipeline_run.py` publishes one writing FIBO `Account` and `TRANSACTED`
   under `pole`, and the Ledger demo's five committed recipes (`packages/demo_fixtures/ledger_*`)
   write FIBO types with no pipeline at all; all load, since the deployment applies the core
   composed with every pack (ADR-108 Amendment 4). So the packs a recipe pins are the union of the
   packs its domain-model nodes name (the core excluded) and the packs that **define** an entity or
   link type its row template writes, `on_match: reference` and conditional entities included.
   Widening (`extends: true`) does not count: it only adds link ends, and a pack-typed end is an
   entity the row template writes, which pins its pack already, so a `TRANSACTED` between two core
   `Endpoint`s rightly pins nothing. Today everything a recipe writes outside its row template is a
   core type (an entity's content `Document` and `HOLDS`; extract's people, organisations, places,
   endpoints and `MENTIONED_IN`; enrich's `SAME_AS`); a future stage that writes a pack type joins
   the union. Publish and the backfill stamp exactly that union, never an extra pin; the engine
   checks that same union and ignores any other pin a hand-written recipe carries, even on a pack
   the ontology it is handed does not compose.
2. **The composed ontology records which pack defines each type.** `OntologySchema` gains
   `type_packs`, a map from every entity and link type a pack defines (not widens) to that pack's
   name, filled by `compose_with_packs` and served with the rest of the schema; the engine, publish
   and the backfill read the union from the ontology they are handed, never from the pack files, so
   the check cannot disagree with the schema in force.
3. **The committed recipes that write pack types are pinned in the same change.** The five Ledger
   recipes gain `pack_versions: {fibo: 1}`. No other committed recipe writes or names a pack (the
   six of the older prison fixture write only core types and are not touched), so D10's "no
   committed recipe names NIEM, so the bump flags no file in the tree" still holds under "names or
   writes". The engine's pin check is its own function, `check_recipe_pins(recipe, ontology)`
   (`services/ingest/engine.py`), which `run_recipe` calls and only `run_recipe`: the dry run,
   Verify and Map previews of a draft are never pin-checked, since a draft is not yet pinned. A test
   finds every committed recipe in the repository by content (a top-level `row_template`), in
   `OspreyFlow_Core` and in `OspreyFlow_Build`'s test fixtures alike, asserts that the set found
   includes the five Ledger recipes, and runs each through `check_recipe_pins` against the
   deployment ontology, so the claim that no recipe that loads today is refused is checked, not
   asserted.
4. **A legacy recipe that pins nothing is stamped with an empty map.** The backfill stamps every
   published row with no `pack_versions`, including one whose recipe names and writes no pack (it is
   stamped `{}`), so it is not read again at every start. Only published rows are read; a row that
   already carries pins, or is a draft, flagged or superseded, is never read or changed.
5. **`pack_versions` is required at publish.** `build_recipe` and the store's `publish` take it with
   no default, so a fresh publish can never store "not pinned" and be mistaken for a legacy row by
   the next start's backfill. A recipe that names or writes a pack and pins an empty map, or a map
   without that pack, is refused by the engine as one pinned at a differing version.
6. **Start-up is one named, tested step.** `reconcile_recipe_pins(store, ontology, read_recipe)`
   (`services/api/studio_recipes.py`) runs the backfill and then `flag_stale(ontology.version,
   ontology.packs)`, and the application's start-up calls it in place of the bare `flag_stale`; the
   start-up reader joins the recipe repository root to a row's `git_path` and turns a missing or
   malformed file into "unreadable", so that row is flagged. The publish route computes the pins
   from the live ontology. A real start-up is tested too, so a start-up that skipped the backfill or
   passed no pack versions would fail.

Tests: `tests/ingest/test_named_packs.py` (a pipeline's one domain node, with a pack and with an
empty config; the types a row template writes mapped through `type_packs`, a core type and a type a
pack only widens mapping to none); `tests/ontology/test_pack_versions.py` (`type_packs` holds every
type each pack defines and no widened type); `tests/services/api/test_pack_versions_for.py`;
`tests/services/api/test_studio_recipes_store.py` (the backfill leaves pinned, draft and
non-published rows untouched and reads no git path of theirs; legacy NIEM, FIBO, STIX, FIBO-written-
under-`pole` and no-pack rows stamped 2, 1, 1, 1 and `{}`; a NULL-pinned row at the current core
version is never flagged; `publish` without `pack_versions` refused; `reconcile_recipe_pins` against
real files in a recipe repository: the legacy NIEM row stamped 2 and then flagged, a `{"niem": 3}`
row still published, a missing and a malformed file each flagged);
`tests/ingest/test_studio_publish_pipeline.py` (`build_recipe` without `pack_versions` refused);
`tests/ingest/test_recipe_engine_end_to_end.py` (a recipe writing FIBO types under `pole` refused
when it pins `{}` and when it pins `{"niem": 3}`, and run when it pins `{"fibo": 1}`; one naming no
pack and pinning `{}` runs on the deployment ontology);
`tests/services/api/test_studio_publish_routes.py` (the route hands `build_recipe` and the store the
pins of the recipe's named and written packs, FIBO under `pole` stamped `{"fibo": 1}`);
`tests/ingest/test_committed_recipes_pin.py` (every committed recipe, found by content in both trees
and including the five Ledger recipes, passes `check_recipe_pins` against the deployment ontology);
`tests/services/api/test_recipe_pins_lifespan.py`, a real Conduit start-up in the shape of
`test_scheduler_lifespan.py` (a legacy NIEM row whose file is under the recipe repository root is
stamped 2 and flagged once the Conduit has started).

### ADR-120, Amendment 2 (23 October 2026) — a run takes the registry row's pins when the committed file has none

Status: **ACCEPTED by the owner, 23 October 2026** ("Yes go ahead"). Decision 1 is his ruling in
chat ("Run takes the row's pins"); decisions 2 and 3 are the coordinator's, accepted with it; decision 2 withdraws a
coordinator ruling that the adversarial review of stage 2's code showed to be wrong.

1. **A run of a published Studio recipe takes the registry row's pins when the committed file has
   none.** The backfill (Amendment 1, decision 4) stamps the `studio_recipes` row, but a run loads
   the committed YAML, and a file committed before ADR-120 carries no `pack_versions`, so
   `check_recipe_pins` would refuse every legacy recipe that writes a pack's types (the AML recipes
   of a deployment that published FIBO pipelines before this record) while its row read as
   published. So every load of a published Studio recipe goes through one function,
   `load_published_recipe(row, repo_root)` in `services/api/studio_publish.py`: it loads the
   committed file and, when that file's `pack_versions` is `None` and the row's is not, takes the
   row's; pins written in the file always win. It is used at all three sites that load a published
   recipe: `run_published_recipe` (which every run reaches: Run now, a scheduled or folder-watch
   run, the administrator's Run now, and each branch of a pipeline run), the pipeline run's own read
   of its shape, and the release of held rows. The file gains its pins the next time the recipe is
   republished. Nothing at start-up writes to the recipe repository. The same fallback also makes a
   Conduit of the old code running beside one of the new safe: a file it re-commits without pins
   still runs on the row's.
2. **A re-commit carries the row's pins as they are, including none; a mapped row with no core
   version is saved without a re-commit.** A schedule change re-commits a published recipe's YAML
   with the row's stored `pack_versions`, never recomputed; a row that has none (for example one
   flagged before ADR-120, which the backfill never reads, or one published by an old-code Conduit
   after the new code's start-up) is re-committed without pins, as before, rather than refused. The
   coordinator's earlier refusal (422 `recipe_not_pinned`, recorded only in `09_INGEST_STUDIO.md`
   and tests) is withdrawn: it stopped an analyst pausing such a recipe. Separately, the Publish
   screen's schedule route saved the schedule and then failed on a row with a mapping and no
   `ontology_version`; it now does what the administrator's route already does, saving the schedule
   and skipping the re-commit. Nothing unpinned that names or writes a pack can run:
   `check_recipe_pins` refuses it in the engine, whatever route reaches it, held-row release
   included (which checks clearance, not status).
3. **Only `build_recipe` widens.** Its `pack_versions` becomes `dict[str, int] | None`, still with
   no default, so a re-commit can pass a row's `None`; the store's `publish` keeps `dict[str, int]`
   and refuses `None`, so Amendment 1's decision 5 holds: a fresh publish never stores "not pinned".

Tests: `tests/ingest/test_studio_publish_pipeline.py` (a backfilled row whose committed file has no
pins runs on the deployment ontology; a file with its own pins wins over the row's; a row and file
both unpinned whose recipe writes FIBO is refused by `StaleRecipeError`; the held rows of a recipe
flagged by a pack bump are refused at release by the engine's pin check);
`tests/services/api/test_load_published_recipe_sites.py` (nothing in `services/api` loads a
published Studio recipe's committed file except through `load_published_recipe`, checked over the
source, and shown red first against two planted loads in the shapes the code uses:
`load_recipe(repo_root / recipe.git_path)` passed straight into another call, and the
conditional-expression form); `tests/services/api/test_studio_recipes_store.py` (`publish` with
`pack_versions=None` refused; `reconcile_recipe_pins` writes nothing under the recipe repository
root); `tests/services/api/test_studio_publish_routes.py` and
`tests/services/api/test_schedule_admin_routes.py` (a schedule change on a row with no pins is saved
and re-committed without pins; one on a pinned row carries them; on the Publish screen's route, a
mapped row with no `ontology_version` is saved and not re-committed, with a 200).

### ADR-120, Amendment 3 (23 October 2026) — a malformed pin value is no pin, and one erratum

Status: **ACCEPTED by the owner, 23 October 2026** ("I accept Amendment 3"). Both are the
coordinator's, from the adversarial review of stage 2's tests, put to the owner at the stage gate.

1. **A `pack_versions` value that is not a JSON object is treated exactly as no pins; an object
   whose values are not all whole numbers is flagged.** A row's column can hold a JSON `null`, a
   scalar or an array (written by hand, or by a bug), which neither decision of Amendment 1 gives a
   meaning. It is read as `None`, `flag_stale` never flags on it, and the backfill stamps it as a
   legacy row (it selects `pack_versions IS NULL OR jsonb_typeof(pack_versions) <> 'object'`), so it
   is pinned at the next start like any other row published before ADR-120. An object with a value
   that is not a JSON whole number (`{"fibo": "x"}`, `{"fibo": "1"}` or `{"fibo": 1.0}`, which only
   look like the loaded version) is read as `None` too, but it is not re-stamped: `flag_stale` flags
   a row any of whose pinned values is not a JSON whole number as well as one whose value differs,
   so the start-up flagging flags it, and it cannot run until it is republished. Nothing that reads
   the column can be stopped by such a value: neither a read of the row nor the start-up flagging.
2. **Erratum to Amendment 2's Tests line.** The held-rows test ("the held rows of a recipe flagged
   by a pack bump are refused at release by the engine's pin check") is in
   `tests/ingest/test_typology_rules.py`, as
   `test_held_rows_are_refused_at_release_when_their_pack_pin_is_stale`, beside the other held-row
   release tests, not in `tests/ingest/test_studio_publish_pipeline.py`; it holds rows and releases
   them with a pin behind the loaded pack, so nothing is flagged in it and the engine is the guard,
   which is all Amendment 2's decision 2 claims. The source check of
   `tests/services/api/test_load_published_recipe_sites.py` is an allow-list: within `services/api`,
   `load_recipe` (under any import name), `Recipe.model_validate`, `Recipe.model_validate_json` and
   `Recipe.model_construct` may be called only in `load_published_recipe`
   (`services/api/studio_publish.py`), in `set_site_grid` (`services/api/app.py`, which loads the
   committed site-grid recipe by fixed path), and in `recipe_reader`
   (`services/api/studio_recipes.py`), the start-up backfill's reader, which reads a published row's
   committed file only to learn which packs the recipe names or writes, for a row that has no pins
   to fall back on. Building a `Recipe(...)` directly (how publish and Verify build one in memory)
   and dynamic `getattr` access are outside the check, which says so.

Tests: `tests/services/api/test_studio_recipes_store.py` (a JSON `null` and an array read as `None`,
do not break flagging, and are stamped by the start-up reconcile; an object with a non-integer
value, one with a numeric string and one with a decimal `1.0`, read as `None`, are not re-stamped,
and are flagged at start-up); `tests/services/api/test_load_published_recipe_sites.py` (one planted
violation per shape the allow-list catches).

### ADR-120, Amendment 4 (23 October 2026) — a self-loop's mutual-information term is 0

Status: **ACCEPTED by the owner, 23 October 2026**: decision 1 from options put to him ("Self-loop's
PMI term is 0"), decisions 2 to 4, the coordinator's, at stage 3's gate ("Accept Amendment 4 - Yes I
do"); decisions 2 to 4 were revised in place after the adversarial reviews of stage 3's tests and
code, before that ruling. Found by stage 3's property test before any of D3's code was written.

1. **A self-loop's mutual-information term is 0.** A link from a node to itself is counted twice in
   that node's degree, so in a small corpus its normalised PMI falls as its occurrences rise, and
   the same-pair invariant D3 states (adding occurrences never lowers a weight) failed for it on the
   property-test grid (for example a cell-share self-loop, 22 to 23 occurrences, 0.89696 to
   0.89695); every pair of distinct nodes held. A link to itself says nothing about a pair of
   distinct nodes, so its term is 0 and its weight follows its count and recency only, which makes
   the invariant hold for every link. The weight's stored inputs do not say whether a link is a
   self-loop, so `compute_weight` takes a required `self_loop` argument that every caller (the
   adapter, the bulk loader, `scripts/compare_vaults.py`) passes.
2. **A self-loop counts twice in its node's degree on every path, and `scripts/compare_vaults.py`
   recomputes with the store's own rules.** The bulk loader counted a self-loop's occurrences twice
   and the store's `bothE()` reads it back twice, but an upsert added the write's occurrences to the
   degree once, so the same self-loop stored different corpus counts by path. The upsert now counts
   it twice, as the bulk loader does. `compare_vaults` passes the link's type (it compares
   `TRANSACTED` links) and `self_loop`, counts a self-loop twice as the store does (it counted it
   once), and recomputes each weight under the version its stored `parameter_set` names (from the
   weights file's history); a `parameter_set` naming a version the file lacks, or a rule other than
   `TRANSACTED`'s, is a mismatch. A component with no `parameter_set` (written before ADR-120,
   perhaps by an upsert that counted a self-loop once) is skipped entirely, neither its counts nor
   its weight compared, and is listed as legacy.
3. **The weights loader refuses a malformed file by name.** It refuses, with `OntologyError` naming
   the version and the field: YAML that does not parse or cannot be constructed; a missing or empty
   `versions`, or a version, `default`, `rules` or rule that is not a mapping; versions that are not
   the integers 1, 2, ... in order (a `true`, `1.0` or `1.5` is not); a missing, non-numeric or
   non-finite parameter (NaN or infinity); α at or below 0, or β or γ below 0 (a non-positive α
   inverts the curve and would silently break the same-pair invariant); a `half_life_days` at or
   below 0; a `midpoint` or `scale` that is not the one derived from α and β; a rule that sets both
   or neither of `heavy` and `fixed`, sets `heavy` below 1 or not a whole number (a YAML `12.0` is a
   whole number), or sets `fixed` outside (0, 1]; and a key it does not know, or a key repeated
   within a mapping. A fixed default rule is allowed (the formula handles it). A rule naming a link
   type no ontology composes is not refused (the weights file is read before and apart from the
   ontology); such a type simply never occurs.
4. **Two things this amendment records rather than changes.** The Verify dry run shows an indicative
   weight (`min(1, occurrences / 5)`) for links it has not stored; it is a preview, never stored or
   compared, and the Glass draws the rules' weight once a link is written. The brief's check that,
   on the PID's own principal star, the coordinator's calls and the shared payer's transfers rank
   among the heaviest and a one-off cell share and the picture among the lightest is made in stage 5
   against the generated case (`tests/scenarios/test_pid_files.py`); stage 3 proves the same
   ordering on a synthetic star.

Tests: `tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_weight_rules.py` (the same-pair invariant over the grid,
self-loop series included, with a self-loop's term 0, and shown able to fail with the term left in;
`npmi`'s edge cases; calibration for every rule; every refusal of decision 3, each naming its
version and field, and a fixed default and a YAML `12.0` accepted);
`tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_counting_store_self_loop.py` and `test_bulk_edge_loader.py` (the
test stores count a self-loop twice as `bothE` does; a self-loop stored alike by both paths; a
second write of it counted twice); `tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_legacy_weight_components.py`
(a component without `parameter_set` reads as `None`); `tests/conformance/graph_port/test_suite.py`
and `test_bulk_loader.py` (a self-loop counted twice on every path, its weight the rules' with
`self_loop` set; a superseded link's component; bulk and upsert alike);
`tests/services/api/working_set/test_link_weight_on_the_wire.py` (the weight the Conduit serialises
is the stored weight); `tests/test_compare_vaults.py` (the recompute uses the store's rules and
counts a self-loop twice; each weight recomputed under the version its `parameter_set` names; an
unknown version and another rule are mismatches; a legacy component is skipped and listed).

### ADR-120, Amendment 5 (23 October 2026) — the corpus counts leave out superseded links, and a backup carries the weights file

Status: **ACCEPTED by the owner, 23 October 2026** ("go ahead with the best course of action that
you decide"), on two findings of stage 3's code review put to him at its gate.

1. **A superseded link does not count in the corpus.** The degree and total queries behind a weight
   filtered only `reverted` links, while every read excludes a link with `superseded_by`; a
   superseded link's occurrences live on in its successor, so counting both counted them twice, and
   `supersede_edge` weighed the replacement against counts that included the link it replaced. The
   corpus counts (the adapter's upsert and supersede, the bulk loader's `degrees` and total, and
   `scripts/compare_vaults.py`) now leave out a link that is reverted or superseded, as reads do.
   Weights already stored keep their value (ADR-120 D3).
2. **A backup carries the weights file and names its version.** `harness/backup.py` copies the
   ontology and the handling scheme so a restore is reproducible; it now copies
   `packages/ontology/weights/default.yaml` too and records the weights file's latest version beside
   the other schema versions, so a restore into a checkout whose weights file lacks a version that
   stored weights name can be detected. The backup tests are fake-driven; this is not proven against
   a live deployment by this record.

Tests: `tests/conformance/graph_port/test_suite.py` and
`tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_bulk_edge_loader.py` (a superseded link's occurrences are not in
its ends' degrees or the type's total, on every path); `tests/test_compare_vaults.py` (the recompute
leaves out superseded links); the harness backup tests (the weights file is in the configuration
sources and its version is recorded).

### ADR-120, Amendment 6 (23 October 2026) — a backup records the weights version; it does not refuse a restore

Status: **ACCEPTED** under the owner's ruling of 23 October 2026 on Amendment 5 ("go ahead with the
best course of action that you decide"); a correction of that amendment's text, made before any of
its code.

Amendment 5 decision 2 said a backup records the weights file's version "so a restore into a
checkout whose weights file lacks a version that stored weights name can be detected". Nothing
detects it: `harness/restore.py`'s compatibility check reads the ontology version only, and a
refusal there is restore behaviour that this project proves live, not by fakes. So the version is
recorded in the backup's schema versions (key `weights`) and the weights file is carried
(`config/weights.yaml`) for an operator to compare; a restore that refuses on it is its own record.

Tests: the harness backup tests (the key `weights` holds the file's latest version; the file is
copied and checksummed).

### ADR-120, Amendment 7 (23 October 2026) — a throw-over's position, yard and item ride on its `OCCURRED_AT` link, and the principal's star is his payment and call circle

Status: **ACCEPTED by the owner, 23 October 2026** ("Accept Amendment 7, put them in version 3
in place"). Found while designing stage 4's plan, before any of its code; adversarially reviewed
three times before the owner saw it.

1. **`OCCURRED_AT` declares four optional properties in NIEM version 3: `lat` and `lon` (`float`),
   `yard` and `item_type` (`string`).**
   - **Why the brief needs them.** The brief contradicts itself here: §5.2 gives `OCCURRED_AT` no
     properties, and §5.7 requires throw-over events to carry the yard's latitude and longitude
     and the properties `yard` and `item_type`. D1 followed §5.2.
   - **Where the code reads them.** On the recipe path an event takes its position only from its
     link's properties (`services/ingest/engine.py`, the `EventRecord` of a temporal link reads
     `properties.get("lat")` and `properties.get("lon")`). A text value becomes a number only for a
     property declared numeric (`_coerce_declared_numeric_types`), and anything that is not a
     number is dropped to no position (`_as_float`). A link property its type does not declare is
     refused by the graph adapter and the bulk loader (`validate_properties`,
     `packages/ontology/validation.py`, called from `graph_arcadedb/adapter.py` and `bulk.py`).
   - **What reads them.** The position is what the map's heat layer, snail trail and site-grid
     geocode read; each selects events with a position. `yard` and `item_type` are what Trends can
     split or filter by, because Trends offers only the properties an event's link type declares
     (`services/api/trends.py`, `trend_options`). The hotspot cells and the weekday-by-hour view
     need none of the four: they bucket by the event's target place and by its time.
   - **What stays unchanged.** None of the four is required, so a find or an assault placed in a
     cell carries none.
   - **Side effects accepted.** Trends also offers `lat` and `lon` as numbers to sum. The
     link-change form lists them as editable, though editing one does not move a stored event.
   - **Duplicated facts.** `yard` repeats the event's target place and `item_type` repeats the
     incident's `item`. The plan test checks that each pair agrees. After a recipe load the
     incident holds an `item` only if Brief 2's throw-over recipe (R10) binds one, so R10 binds
     `item` from the same column as `item_type`.

   **They go into version 3 itself, not a version 4.**
   - **The house rule.** A content change bumps the version (`default.yaml`'s own history), because
     a bump is what flags the recipes pinned to the old content and stops a stale run. That
     protects content something has loaded or pinned.
   - **Nothing has loaded or pinned version 3.**
     - It has never been pushed: the last push to `origin/main` was on 20 October, and version 3
       was committed on 23 October.
     - The owner's running deployment holds version 2. Its image was built on 20 October, it
       mounts no `packages/` path, and its `niem.yaml` reads `pack_version: 2`.
     - The throwaway test stack runs no service of its own, and its tests read the pack from the
       checkout.
     - No committed recipe writes `OCCURRED_AT`.
     - No snapshot or hash of version 3 exists anywhere. A store that applied the old version 3
       holds nothing the new one conflicts with: its schema declares only the indexed properties,
       each created `IF NOT EXISTS`.
   - **The risk that remains.** An environment that loads version 3 before this change and then
     runs a recipe written after it. That recipe would pass the pin check, and its run would then
     fail outright at its first `OCCURRED_AT` write, committing nothing. So no image is rebuilt
     (`ospreyflow start --build`) and no stack is rebuilt from this checkout until `niem.yaml`
     carries the four properties.
   - **Additions only still holds.** Version 3 stays a strict superset of version 2, which is all
     D1's "additions only" test compares.
   - **Where else this lands.** `01_DOMAIN_MODEL.md`'s NIEM version 3 paragraph names the four
     properties. Brief 2's throw-over file (R10) gains `lat` and `lon` columns. Its `recovered`
     column is declared nowhere and is that brief's to settle.

2. **"The principal's star" in the weight check is his payment and call circle.**
   - **The problem.** D3's Tests line and Amendment 4 decision 4 ask that, on the principal's star,
     the coordinator's call link and the shared payer's transfer links rank among the heaviest,
     and a one-off cell share and his picture link among the lightest. A call joins `Endpoint` to
     `Endpoint`, and a transfer joins `Asset` or `Endpoint` to `Asset` or `Endpoint`
     (`default.yaml`: `COMMUNICATED_WITH`, `TRANSACTED`). So neither touches his `Person` node,
     and on his own links the check cannot be made.
   - **The circle.** The check is made on his circle as the demo analyst sees it, the `SECRET`
     link excluded. The circle holds:
     - his own links;
     - every link of each endpoint he uses (his PIN account and his private-cash account);
     - every link of each endpoint that those exchange calls or money with (here the
       coordinator's number, the unidentified number and the payer's account).

     It holds about 62 links, including all three of the payer's transfers and the relays' calls
     to the coordinator.
   - **The thresholds.** A heavy-end place is counted from the heavy end and a light-end place
     from the light end; either way, a tie takes the worse place. A fraction of the circle rounds
     up.
     - The coordinator's call link from his PIN account ranks in the top three. The plan makes
       him the coordinator's heaviest caller by a margin: at least 40 calls more than each relay
       over the window (9 a week against 7 from December 2025). The margin is needed because his
       PIN account also calls the unidentified number, which lowers his link's mutual information
       slightly.
     - Each of the payer's three transfer links ranks in the top quarter.
     - His picture link and his one-week cell share both rank in the bottom eighth.
   - **The test, and the dates it holds at.** The binding test is stage 5's, against a real load
     of the generated case into a store that holds that case alone. It asserts the thresholds at
     three points:
     - on the weights as stored at load, which are the weights the canvas draws (each is computed
       with the time of the write);
     - recomputed by the store's own `compute_weight` from the stored components, with `now` at
       the intelligence cut-off (30 April 2026 23:59:59 UTC);
     - recomputed the same way with every temporal link's end far in the past (recency halves
       every 90 days and never reaches 0).

     So the result does not depend on the day the case is loaded. That test re-counts nothing; it
     reads the store's components and so inherits Amendments 4 and 5's counting. The standard
     demo store also holds other datasets' links of the same types, and its larger per-type
     totals raise an exclusive pair's mutual information. For the heavy-end thresholds the
     case-only store is therefore the harder one. For the light end it is slightly the easier: the
     demo store's other prison data adds cell shares, which lifts the one-week share a little
     (about 0.01 raw).
   - **The arithmetic** (D3: "checked by arithmetic before it is built"). It uses the real rules
     (weights file version 1) and the real function, on per-type counts estimated from the
     stage 4 design for all 62 links. Across the three points:
     - the call link places 1st;
     - the transfers place 8th to 15th (the top quarter is 16);
     - the picture is the lightest;
     - the one-week cell share is at most 5th from the bottom (the bottom eighth is 8).

     An earlier draft proposed "the two lightest", and it fails here: the three inferred
     `PASSES_ITEMS_TO` links, one occurrence each, fall below the cell share once recency fades.
   - **Shown red against planted wrong rules** (rule 15; the brief asks for this in §6). Each
     plant turns the check red at all three points:
     - `TRANSACTED` with heavy 60 (ten times too heavy): the transfers fall to 18th–44th.
     - `SHARED_CELL_WITH` with heavy 1: the one-week cell share rises to 40th or higher from the
       light end.
     - `COMMUNICATED_WITH` with heavy 4,000: the call link falls to 12th–23rd.

     At the cut-off point alone, a looser "top third" would have let the first plant pass, because
     recency lifts every April link. That is why the threshold is the top quarter.
   - **The stage 4 check.** Stage 4's plan test repeats this arithmetic on the plan's own per-type
     counts. It is advisory: with no store it has to count, and it counts as Amendments 4 and 5 do
     (a self-loop twice, a superseded link not at all).
   - **J1 is unchanged.** J1's 49 counts his own links only, as "With all links" does.

Tests:
- `tests/ontology/test_niem_pack_v3.py`, shown red before `niem.yaml` changes:
  - `OCCURRED_AT` declares the four properties with those types, and none is required.
  - An `OCCURRED_AT` write with `lat`, `lon`, `yard` and `item_type` passes `validate_properties`.
  - One with an undeclared key is still refused.
  - Version 3 is still a superset of version 2.
- `tests/ingest/test_occurred_at_event_position.py`, through `run_recipe`:
  - **The fake graph port.** It is bound to `load_deployment_ontology()` (core and NIEM), not the
    core alone. It refuses an unknown type, an undeclared property and a link whose ends its type
    does not allow, as the graph adapter does.
  - **The recipe.** It pins `{"niem": 3}` and binds text values, as a CSV gives them.
  - **What it asserts.** An `OCCURRED_AT` row's event carries `lat` and `lon` as floats, and
    `yard` and `item_type` in its properties. A recipe that also binds an undeclared `recovered`
    on the link fails: `run_recipe` raises `OntologyError` at the graph write, and nothing is
    committed. Resolution checks only declared properties, so this is not a row rejection.
  - **Shown red.** The ontology passed to `run_recipe` declares both `lat` and `lon` as `string`.
    The event then still exists, with no position. (Declaring one alone fails by a different path:
    an event refuses one coordinate without the other.)
- `tests/services/api/test_trends.py`: `trend_options` over `load_deployment_ontology()` offers
  `yard` and `item_type` for `OCCURRED_AT`.
- `tests/scenarios/test_pid_plan.py`:
  - All 262 throw-over `OCCURRED_AT` links carry the four properties.
  - Each link's `yard` names its target yard.
  - Each link's `item_type` equals its incident's `item`.
  - The item multiset holds.
  - Every property the plan writes is declared on its type.
  - Decision 2's thresholds hold on the plan's counts (advisory).
- `tests/scenarios/test_pid_files.py` (stage 5): decision 2's thresholds at the three points, from a
  real load. It is shown red with each of the three plants above.

### ADR-120, Amendment 8 (23 October 2026) — what the generated case holds, who loads it, and when the script's figures are true

Status: **ACCEPTED by the owner, 23 October 2026** ("I accept Amendment 8"); adversarially reviewed
three times before he saw it. Decisions 1 to 4 are the owner's rulings of 23 October, from options
put to him. Decisions 5 to 11 are the coordinator's design of stage 4's plan within the brief. They are
recorded here because stage 4's review found them held only in working notes (rule 11).

1. **The script's Act 1 figures are those of the seeded case; the brief's hold once chapter 4 has
   loaded the reports** (the owner: "Keep plan, fix script"). Brief 2 loads every intelligence
   report live in chapter 4 (R9), so in Act 1 no report exists. The plan gives every link the
   moment it is loaded. The seed loads most links. Chapter 4 loads every report and every link that
   touches one. Chapter 9 loads the second seized-handset batch. The plan test proves each figure
   at both the seed and chapter 4 moments:
   - J1, the principal's links as the analyst sees them, is 45 in Act 1 and 49 after chapter 4
     (46 and 50 cleared to SECRET). The four reports that name him add the other four.
   - J5's principal and relay_4 are 2 degrees apart in both, by 5 routes in Act 1 and 6 after
     chapter 4. One route runs through a report.
   - J7 ranks the principal first at about 0.87 in both, at least twice the second, then the three
     relays who call the coordinator.

   The figures hold until chapter 5's reviewer accepts a duplicate person (`SAME_AS`, collapsed at
   query time, rule 6), which can add links to his star. The script's Act 1 lines change to 45 and
   5; `PID_ACTUALS.md` records both moments.

2. **Outsiders, as Brief 2's identity rules have them** (the owner: "Reshape the story").
   - **Identifiers.** Every person who is not a prisoner carries a `QQ` National Insurance number.
     Prisoners carry a prison number. A report names a prisoner by prison number and anyone else by
     National Insurance number, which needs a Brief 2 addition (decision 3).
   - **Associations.** An association or family link joins two prisoners only. The principal's six
     outside associates become visitors, two visits each.
   - **Removed.** No seized-media extract `Document` and no `HOLDS` exist.
   - **Seized handsets.** A seized handset is paired with its SIM. The SIM's calls are recorded,
     and the handset is used by the prisoner it was found with, or by nobody.
   - **The arrested person.** His handset is found with nobody, and its SIM calls the number
     nobody owns. He joins the principal through a chapter 4 report that names them both, no longer
     through his phone (brief §5.4). The report's text records the handset, the contact "Cally V",
     the bank account found on it and the calls.
   - **The found account.** It is on no entity, only in that report's text, so it has no holder by
     construction (the third gap).

3. **Brief 1's plan defines what the case holds; Brief 2 gains whatever it cannot yet load** (the
   owner: "Plan defines; Brief 2 adds").
   - **The contract.** The plan exports `LOAD_SHAPES` and `ENTITY_SHAPES`. A link shape is its
     type, its two ends and its properties. An end is an entity type, narrowed where several recipes
     write one type: an endpoint by its kind, an incident as a throw-over or not, a place by its
     kind. An entity shape is a discriminated type and its properties. Each row also gives the file and columns stage 5 writes for it,
     the recipe that loads it, and whether its handling is the recipe's or comes from columns of
     the row. Where Brief 2 as written cannot load it, the row also gives one sentence naming what
     Brief 2 must add.
   - **Exceptions.** The two ways ADR-120 already writes outside a recipe are rows of their own:
     D8's `PASSES_ITEMS_TO` through the graph port, and D9's pictures through the picture route.
   - **The additions found so far:**
     - the conflict links, including the `SECRET` one, which carry the access demonstration;
     - a person's use of a phone number;
     - a throw-over's mention in its day's reports;
     - reports with more than one area, and with their own owning unit;
     - places beyond the five kinds R11 has, and a second parent (the zone);
     - custody and cell stays with separate intervals, and no `PART_OF` beyond the plan's;
     - report subjects named by National Insurance number as well as prison number;
     - handling from the row, wherever one file holds rows of both units;
     - an optional "found with" on a seized handset;
     - a cell share's last day, not its last week's Monday;
     - entity properties no column carries yet: a visitor's date of birth, a person's aliases and
       a throw-over's name;
     - a background visitor's ownership of the number their prisoner calls.
   - **The test.** Every link and every entity the plan holds must match exactly one shape, so a
     shape nobody can load fails the plan test before stage 5 writes a file. Every file whose rows
     carry more than one handling must take it from columns. The list of additions in the test is a
     record for Brief 2, not a proof. Amendment 7 had already widened Brief 2's throw-over file in the same way.

4. **J8's limit is not shown on the Prison Intelligence Dataset** (the owner: "Keep 3,000/30,000").
   - **Why.** The working-set cap is 50,000 nodes and 250,000 links (ADR-007). The scale case holds
     about 9,500 nodes and 30,000 links, so no expand in it can breach the cap.
   - **What the scale cohort proves.** The grouped opening only. The plan test asserts it holds
     fewer than 50,000 nodes.
   - **What follows.** The limit scene is the script's to move or drop.

5. **J7's working set is the principal with all links, then the coordinator's number with all
   links** (the script's J2 move).
   - **Why the star alone fails.** Every node is next to the principal, so a relay bridges almost nothing.
     Measured on the cast's star alone (the coordinator's scratch `cast_reshaped_star.py`, after
     chapter 4), the principal scores 0.89. The establishment, which holds every prisoner, is second
     at 0.03, and relay_1 scores under 0.01.
   - **The figure.** The principal's betweenness on the defined set is about 0.87, not the
     script's 0.55. `PID_ACTUALS.md` reports the plan's figure.
   - **The named relay.** J5's relay is relay_4.

6. **The cast's working names change where they collide, and the Calder Street Group has seven
   members.**
   - **The renames.**
     - The brief's names are placeholders. Two of them are surnames in the older synthetic prison
       fixture (OKAFOR; DUNMORE, which the brief used as a group name).
     - "Kestrel" names a company in the Ledger fixture and an entry in the synthetic screening
       list.
     - They become Darren Ashcombe, the Calder Street Group and the Larkhill Lane Group.
   - **Why seven.** The brief puts 13 group members among the 28 prisoners the illicit-item reports
     name, but its groups hold 13 people including the third member, whom no report names. So one
     group must hold one more.
   - **Names stay unique.** Every name the plan gives (family names, staff, groups, establishments,
     the zone) is absent from every other demo fixture.

7. **The 229 reports are one query-builder pattern through a zone place.**
   - **The zone.** A `Location` "Wing F and its yards" has Wing F and the four hotspot yards
     `PART_OF` it.
   - **How a report is tied to a day.** A throw-over is `MENTIONED_IN` every report of its day whose
     area its yard serves.
   - **The pattern.** It runs: area `PART_OF` zone, area `MENTIONED_IN` report, throw-over
     `MENTIONED_IN` report, throw-over `OCCURRED_AT` yard, and yard `PART_OF` zone (a join).
   - **Why yard reports name Wing F too.** The pattern binds distinct nodes to its three `Location`
     variables (zone, area, yard), so a yard report also names Wing F, the wing its yard serves.
     Without that, a yard report whose day's only hotspot throw-over was in its own yard would be
     missed.
   - **The test.** The plan test compiles the pattern with the real builder and proves it selects
     the same 229 as the brief's rule.

8. **The picture tests are stage 5's.** D9's Tests line puts the picture byte, size and
   reproducibility tests in `tests/scenarios/test_pid_plan.py`. The plan names the picture subjects
   and their `DEPICTS` links (its test checks that each has exactly one). The bytes are drawn in
   stage 5, so those tests are `tests/scenarios/test_pid_files.py`'s.

9. **Erratum to Amendment 7 decision 2, and the moment its check is made at.**
   - **The margin.** "At least 40 calls more than each relay over the window (9 a week against 7
     from December 2025)" means over the call period, 1 September 2025 to 30 April 2026, as its
     own parenthesis says. Over March and April alone the margin is about 17. The plan gives the
     principal 201 calls to the coordinator's number and each relay 158.
   - **The moment.** The circle is weighed at both the seed and chapter 4 moments, and the
     thresholds must hold at both. Stage 5 checks Amendment 7's three points (as stored, at the
     cut-off, and with every end far in the past) at each moment. The circle holds about 58 links at the seed and about 62 after
     chapter 4. The arithmetic is re-run on the reshaped plan by its test.

10. **Synthetic by construction, extended** (D4 and D5).
    - **Bank accounts.** The background's are drawn from `SYN-70000` to `SYN-79999`, clear of the
      older fixture's. The cast's two (the payer's `SYN-00417` and the found `SYN-00988`) are
      fixed.
    - **SIM identities.** They use the test network `00101`.
    - **Disjoint from other fixtures.** Every bank account, private-cash and PIN reference,
      National Insurance number (`[A-Z]{2}\d{6}[A-D]`) and prison number (`[A-Z]\d{4}[A-Z]{2}`)
      the plan gives is absent from what every other fixture's and seed's own generator produces.
      The plan test runs those generators, as it does for phones.
    - **The ownerless number.** It moves out of `07700 900777`, which three test files use, into the
      PID's 900600–900899 block. A test searches the repository's tests, apps, packages and scripts
      (the PID's own files aside) and finds it in none, nor the coordinator's number.
    - **Brief 2's bad-number teaching row.** It uses `07700 900 6O3`, which corrects to
      +447700900603, one of the background numbers: a mistyped background number, as an analyst would
      meet one.

11. **Smaller rules of the plan.**
    - **Finds.** A find's `ROLE_IN` gives role "occupant" to every person in the cell on the
      find's date: the principal and relay_1 for the two finds in their cell.
    - **Handling.** A link's handling is the regional unit's when either end belongs to the regional
      unit, and Fenwick Moor's own otherwise. The one `SECRET` link is the exception, set by hand.
    - **Cast and background.** The background touches the cast only in these ways:
      - the group members and the four former cell-mates may share cells with background
        prisoners (never in a cast cell; the principal, the relays, the brother and the third
        member share with nobody but as the cast table says);
      - sixteen cast PIN accounts and the seized SIMs call background numbers;
      - structural links, report mentions and pictures.
    - **Custody and places.** Every prisoner has exactly one open custody and one open cell at the
      cut-off, and a closed stay carries its end date; counts "at the cut-off" use the open ones. Apart
      from the cast table's own F2 cells (the principal, the relays), no cast prisoner is on landing
      F2, so the bulk list is exactly F2's 40. Every incident of the
      demo case has exactly one place. A unit follows the establishment in both profiles: Fenwick
      Moor's data is local, and every other establishment's, with its visitors, incidents and
      accounts, is regional.
    - **Report numbers and dates.** The plan holds 350 reports: 229 selected, and 121 not (40 in
      the zone before the throw-over window, 81 elsewhere). A report's date is its `sent_at`, which
      Brief 2's `submitted_at` column carries.
    - **The bulk list.** It is `bulk_list(plan)`, not a constant.

Tests: `tests/scenarios/test_pid_plan.py`:

- decision 2's shapes (the found account in one text and on no entity, a seized handset used only
