**Phase 8's exit is met:** the full prototype pipeline runs, and its run report discloses both expert
steps (`test_phase8_exit.py`; the live walk under the lease named in the lane's report).

**Not built.** DuckDB time and peak memory per SQL step in the metering (phase 10's). The SQL step's
columns are not offered in the Map editor from the static gate: they come from its live sample, as
every step's do. A fuzzy match's comparison vector carries its settings, not Splink's per-comparison
levels.

### ADR-147, Amendment 2 (9 November 2026) — the owner's map rulings: Java in the Conduit, gazetteer places copied into a case, the gazetteer's unit a build setting

Status: accepted 9 November 2026; the owner's rulings 1, 6 and 8 of that day (`process/lanes/MORNING.md`,
"Your rulings, 9 November"); every other choice the platform lane's, under Prompt L's rule
(`process/lanes/platform/REPORT.md`, "Decisions taken"). Written by the platform lane in P5. ADR-099,
ADR-014–017, ADR-147 and its Amendment 1 are otherwise unchanged.

**Context.** Three questions P3 and P4 left with the owner: Java 21, which planetiler needs, was kept out
of the Conduit's image because its only runtime here, Eclipse Temurin, is GPL-2.0 with the Classpath
exception and the licence register passed no GPL; adding the gazetteer to a working case made the case
read a composite, which is read-only for loads (ADR-099 Amendment 15); and the gazetteer's dataset was
held by the recipe's `unit-1`, so a case of any other unit could not add it.

**Decision.**

1. **Java in the Conduit's image (ruling 1, option A).** `services/api/Dockerfile` jlinks a Java 21
   runtime from `eclipse-temurin:21-jdk`, pinned by its digest (the multi-architecture index), into
   `/opt/java` (eighteen modules, no tools, debug symbols, headers or man pages), on the Conduit's
   `PATH`, so *Admin › Maps*' Build finds `java` and runs planetiler in the Conduit; the jar stays the
   owner's, placed by `ospreyflow map build --planetiler-jar`. **The licence register records the one
   exception** (`spec/00_ARCHITECTURE.md` §7): `GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0`, for a runtime
   recorded there, `java` alone. A plain GPL of any version, GPL-3.0 with the exception, a GPL with any
   other exception, and AGPL still never pass. **`make licence-check` reads it**: an image declares a
   runtime it carries by `LABEL org.ospreyflow.runtime.<name>.licence`, which a new leg
   (`tools/licence_check.find_runtime_offenders`) checks over every Dockerfile, and a Java stage, a
   `jlink`, an `/opt/java` or a distribution's Java package with no such label fails too. The labels are
   read however they are written (quoted or not, several on a line, continued, the legacy form).
   **`git`** (GPL-2.0-only, already in the image: the Conduit runs it to publish recipes,
   `09_INGEST_STUDIO.md` §6) is declared the same way, and the register does not pass it. **The owner
   ruled on 9 November 2026:** the `git` command is replaced by dulwich, under its Apache-2.0 licence
   (studio-b's carry in L1.7a), and `git` then leaves the image. Until that carry lands the leg names it on
   every run as **not yet passed** (`AWAITING_OWNER`), with that ruling and carry, never silently, and
   an undeclared `git` fails.
   **trivy does not see the runtime.** A runtime unpacked from Temurin's tarball and derived by `jlink`
   is no distribution package and no jar, so `trivy image` names nothing of it: the same image built
   from Temurin 21.0.1 (October 2023, with known CVEs) scans clean, as the current one does (measured on
   the test server). So **the runtime's version is a gate of its own**
   (`tools/java_runtime_check.py`): the Dockerfile declares it in `LABEL
   org.ospreyflow.runtime.java.version`, beside the licence label. The built image's
   `/opt/java/release` (`JAVA_VERSION`) and `java -version` (its build) must be that version (CI's
   `trivy-image-api` job, after its build). **The Java stage's pinned digest must be the one its tag,
   `eclipse-temurin:21-jdk`, resolves to on Docker Hub now** (Build's `make ci`, after
   `core-check`); a pin older than the tag's current digest is red. Whatever cannot be read (the
   image, the Dockerfile's pinned tag, or Docker Hub's answer) is a refusal, never a pass. **The
   policy, the orchestrator's call on review:** the tag's digest, not Adoptium's release list,
   because the tag moves only once an image exists to repin to. So CI is never red for days with
   nothing to take, and an old commit re-run is red only when its pin is no longer the tag's, never
   merely because a release was announced. Repin the digest and the label together. It needs Docker
   and the network, as the image scans do, and never runs in Core's Makefile, which stands alone
   (ADR-114 Amendment 2). Pinned at **21.0.13+9**, October 2026's update.
   Its bundled native libraries' licences, for the NOTICE, are in `spec/00` §7.
2. **Gazetteer places copied into a case's own dataset (ruling 6, option C).** Adding a gazetteer
   copies its places into a case's own dataset (`services/api/case_gazetteers.py`), so **the case stays
   one dataset and keeps its loads**. **It is a dataset-level action** (the orchestrator's review):
   `PUT`/`DELETE /v1/datasets/{dataset}/gazetteers/{gazetteer}`, behind the dataset route's own gate (a
   person one of whose cases loads into the dataset) and **`run_pipelines`**, the right that runs a load
   into a dataset, the narrowest that may write into it; a composite or a drawn dataset is refused, as for
   any load. **The gazetteer must be of the dataset's own unit**; another unit's is refused with the same
   404 and words as no gazetteer at all, so the answer tells nothing of which regions another unit has
   built. The
   case's `GET /v1/investigations/{id}/map/gazetteers` (Viewer, `investigate`) lists the gazetteers of its
   own dataset's unit and which it holds, by name only, never a count of places.
   - **A copy** is a `Location` of its own (rule 6), its id made from the place's and the dataset's, with
     the place's properties and **the gazetteer's handling**; its one source is the gazetteer
     (`gazetteer:<dataset>`, locator `place`: no node id, path or row, rule 7); and **its provenance names
     the gazetteer** (`Provenance.gazetteer`), kept through every later write by `merge_provenance`:
     the dataset id of the gazetteer it was copied from, always of the copy's own dataset's unit (a
     gazetteer of another unit is never added). **Only a place the gazetteer's dataset holds alone
     is copied** (a node it shares with another dataset is not the gazetteer's place).
     **Decision 3b holds for a copy, keyed on that provenance**, not on a `gazetteer-*` dataset name:
     `ontology.handling.is_gazetteer_held` withholds its source identifiers from every request reader, and
     `builders.match_any_field` matches it on its name alone (`__.values("provenance").select("gazetteer")`
     in the guard). The place search keeps a copy as a gazetteer place.
   - **Recorded for the dataset** (`dataset_gazetteers`), so every case reading it sees the gazetteer
     added; a case deleted or moved leaves the record with the copies.
   - **Copied in pages of 500, each its own transaction**, never one unbounded write; a copy that fails
     part way is finished by copying again (the same nodes). A failed re-add leaves the earlier record.
   - **A copy the case has made its own** (another writer's source, as when a case's own upsert-mode load
     matched and wrote onto it; or a person's confirmation) **is the case's data now: a re-build never
     writes over it**, though the store's merge keeps the newest write. A reference-mode lookup
     (`on_match: reference`, through `find_node`, which 3b leaves unguarded since the identifier is the
     loader's own row's) finds the copy and links to it, writing nothing onto it.
   - **A re-build refreshes the rest**: the Admin route and both command-line builds copy the places again
     into every recorded dataset once the places commit, drop the record of a dataset no longer there
     (never writing into one).
   - **A removal deletes nothing** (the orchestrator's ruling (d) of 9 November 2026, which replaces
     the removal clause of the brief; the owner's ruling 6 named only the copying). Every copy stays,
     whatever rests on it, as the dataset's own, with its gazetteer mark (3b holds); the record is
     kept as removed, so a re-build no longer refreshes it and the place search no longer offers its
     copies (keyed on the mark and the removal record, the same for every copy). The answer says so
     in fixed words and gives no count, so a link a reader may not see (above their clearance, in a
     case's analyst layer) changes nothing they are told or then read (rule 3): there is nothing to
     compare. Adding the gazetteer again takes the record back and re-links the same copies, never a
     second set. **A re-build reverts nothing either**: the copy of a place the gazetteer no longer
     holds stays, as the dataset's own, still offered, since reverting it would carry the same
     signal. No link read at the highest clearance decides anything.
   - **Audited before the copy**: the addition's audit entry is written once the record is, before
     the first page, so a copy that fails part way, its pages committed, is never unaudited.
   - **Failures.** A copy that fails part way leaves its pages committed and the record in place, so
     the dataset is said to hold the gazetteer and adding it again finishes the copy, or removing it
     stops it. Any refresh failure (one dataset's copy, or the records' own read) is said in the
     build's words, naming no dataset, and neither fails the committed build nor skips the datasets
     after it. A removal needs only its record, never the gazetteer's state now; a re-add is
     recorded as the re-adder's. Another unit's gazetteer is refused with the
     same 404 and words as no gazetteer at all, so the answer tells nothing of which regions another
     unit has built. The copier reads as the dataset's own unit, so a restricted code is seen.
   - **Which loads make a copy the case's**: a reference-mode load (the gazetteer recipe's, proven
     live) links to a copy without writing onto it, so it does not; an upsert-mode write onto the
     copy's id, or a confirmation, does (both proven live).
   - **The place search reads the removal records as its dependency**: a Conduit without them
     answers 503, never offering a removed gazetteer's copies again. A removed gazetteer's copies are
     left out after the store's scan, so they count toward its limit, and `more` says so (rule 2).

3. **The gazetteer's unit a build setting (ruling 8).** The recipe's `unit-1` is no longer what a build
   uses: *Admin › Maps*' Build takes a unit (empty: the administrator's own), and `ospreyflow map build`
   and `python -m scripts.build_local_basemap` take `--unit` (required), as does the set-up
   console's Build (a field on its Geospatial screen, refused in words before anything runs
   without one; `harness/geospatial.build_basemap_step`). A unit that holds no case and no
   dataset here, and is not the administrator's own, is refused in words before anything is fetched or
   written (`map_places.check_unit`, `UNKNOWN_UNIT`, which names no other unit); otherwise the places,
   their points and their dataset are that unit's. **A re-build is for the unit the region was first
   built for** (its dataset keeps its first unit, `register`): another is refused in words
   (`OTHER_UNIT`), so a dataset never holds the places of two units. **A unit holding only a
   gazetteer's dataset holds nothing** (`units_held` leaves `gazetteer-*` datasets out).

**Left, and why:**
- **The Glass has no control for a gazetteer yet**: platform's P6 (the orchestrator, 9 November 2026),
  a panel beside the map's place search; until then the case's dataset picker still offers a gazetteer
  dataset as a composite (a carry to the case lane).
- **A case of another unit than the gazetteer's** cannot add it (ADR-099 decision 3); ruling 8 lets an
  administrator build a gazetteer for each unit.
- **The port's own contract and the graph-port conformance suite** (`ports/graph.py`'s `search_nodes`
  and `suggest_nodes`; `tests/conformance/graph_port`) do not yet say that a copy matches on its name
  alone: neither is this lane's file, so the wording and a conformance case
  (`test_a_gazetteer_copy_matches_a_case_reader_on_its_name_alone`) are a request to the orchestrator
  (`process/lanes/platform/PORT_CONTRACT.diff`), proved live with the diff applied, the case red with
  the search guard's copy clause or the suggestion's withholding removed.
- **The version gate's wiring** is in shared files: CI's step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the
  owner's (`process/lanes/platform/P5_ci.diff`), and Build's `make ci` target, the orchestrator's
  (`process/lanes/platform/JAVA_RUNTIME_CI.diff`). Each was shown red over a Temurin 21.0.1 image on
  the test server.
- **A fresh install builds its first basemap from *Admin › Maps*.** With no case or dataset yet,
  the command-line builds and the set-up console's (which runs the command line) refuse every
  unit, since none holds anything and they have no administrator's own unit to admit. *Admin ›
  Maps* admits the administrator's own (`test_a_fresh_install_builds_from_admin_maps_alone`).
  Recorded, not changed: a tiles-only build, without a gazetteer, is the likely next step if the
  console must build first.
- **The image's source offer and NOTICE** for the Java runtime are a release step (`spec/00` §7).
- **The copy is made in the request**, a page at a time; each re-build refreshes every recorded dataset
  inside its stream. Measured under the platform lane's lease on stack a, 9 November 2026 (the
  machine shared with other lanes' runs, load average 13 to 21; the lease covers the stack, not the
  machine): 2,000 planted places in 42.7 s at 08:20 UTC and in 29.7 s at 08:28 UTC, about 15 to 21 s
  per 1,000 (`test_a_region_is_copied_in_bounded_pages_and_timed`). A region of 100,000 places would
  take over twenty minutes per dataset: a background job is the likely next step.
- **planetiler runs under the image's Java** (v0.10.2's `--help`, exit 0, in the built image on amd64,
  the test server), but no real tile build is run in tests (tier 1 only, no real tiles fetched).

**Tests that would fail if it were broken** (each shown red by a plant at its real call site,
`process/lanes/platform/P5_RED_RECORD.md`):
- **Java**: `tests/licence_check/test_runtime_licences.py` (a plain GPL-2.0 Java, GPL-3.0 with the
  exception, another exception, the exception for an unrecorded runtime, an undeclared Java: each
  refused; the real Dockerfiles pass); `tests/test_conduit_image_java_licence.py` (the stage pinned by
  digest, jlinked, declared, on the `PATH`); `tests/licence_check/test_java_runtime_check.py` (the
  version gate: a pin its tag has moved on from, a label drifted from the image by version or by
  build, a release file or `java -version` naming none, a Java stage not pinned by tag and digest,
  every way Docker Hub's answer can fail, the label however written, through `main` and the
  fetch's own code).
- **Copies**: live, `tests/ingest/test_case_gazetteer_copies_live.py` (found by name at its point and a
  SECRET place not; no identifier on a node read, an expansion or a search; never matched by its `osm_id`
  or `uprn`, more than a page sharing the prefix; a re-copy writes no second copy and keeps a place
  gone; a restricted case load on a copy stays the case's at a re-build; a real case load references
  the copies and a refresh after it writes no second set; every page of 2,000 places written; a case load
  writing onto a copy through the real merge keeps it one, withheld; node detail in bulk and the
  type-ahead by name send none; a retracted copy stays one, withheld),
  `tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_every_read_withholds_by_its_principal.py` (every read in the
  adapter's package deserialised with its own caller's principal, through the module or not, and no
  deserialiser imported under another name or handed on as a value, so no read path sends a copy's
  identifier), `test_audit_section_routes.py` (*Audit* shows the dataset alone) and
  `tests/ingest/test_case_gazetteer_routes_live.py` (through the routes: the case stays one dataset
  and the Studio's upload, a load a composite case refuses, is made, and refused once the case reads a
  composite; search, seed, expansion and the type-ahead carry and match no
  identifier; a removal in a case whose copy has a SECRET link and in one whose copies have none,
  answered and then read alike, and a re-add re-linking the same copies); offline, `tests/services/api/test_case_gazetteers_routes.py` (which gazetteers,
  the refusals and their words, what a copy is written as, a removal answering alike whatever rests on a copy (red against the
  build that reverted), another unit's gazetteer answered as none, the dataset's record seen by every
  case reading it, a failed copy keeping its record, one dataset's failed refresh said alone, a
  rebuild skipping a dataset gone), the place search leaving a removed gazetteer's copies out,
  `tests/ontology/test_gazetteer_identifiers_withheld.py` (a copy, and `merge_provenance` keeping it one),
  `tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_gazetteer_name_only_match.py`, `test_map_places_route.py`; the
  routes' rights and levels, `test_route_rights.py` and `test_investigation_levels.py`.
- **The unit**: `test_geospatial_admin_routes.py` (refused in words, nothing built; a named unit's
  places and dataset), `test_gazetteer_build_registration_order.py` (both command-line builds check it
  before anything, and refresh the cases after the registration), `test_gazetteer_dataset_registration.py`,
  `tests/cli/test_map_verb.py`, `Maps.test.tsx`; the set-up console,
  `tests/harness/test_webapp_geospatial.py` (none, an option or a control character refused, nothing
  run; any unit the Conduit can name sent, and its refusal of an unknown one shown in its words; the fake
  runner refusing with the Conduit's own parser) and `GeospatialScreen.test.tsx`.

**Cost.** The Conduit's image grows by the jlinked runtime: 62 MB (`/opt/java`); the image is
1.86 GB on amd64 (1.33 GB measured on arm64). A new `21-jdk` image turns `make ci` red until it is taken. Each
dataset that takes a gazetteer holds a copy of every place, written a page at a time (15 to 21 s per
1,000 places, measured as above), and keeps them after a removal; a re-build rewrites every recorded
dataset's copies but those the case made its own. A removal is one record's update.

### ADR-147, Amendment 3 (10 November 2026) — a gazetteer's own identifiers withheld from every node, and matched on none

**Why.** A gazetteer loaded through the Studio arrives in a case's own dataset as a plain file: nothing marks
it a gazetteer, so Amendment 1 point 3a, which withholds a gazetteer's identifiers from a node in a
`gazetteer-*` dataset or a case's copy of one, left `osm_id` and its kind in that case's node reads (CARRIES
row 23, raised by studio). The owner chose the strict reading (MORNING item 11, option (a)).

**Decisions.**
1. **The six identifiers only a gazetteer carries** (`schemas.mapconfig.GAZETTEER_ONLY_IDENTIFIERS`: `osm_id`,
   `os_place_id`, `gss_code`, `gnis_feature_id`, `tiger_geoid`, `nad_address_id`) **leave every node for every
   request reader**, whatever dataset it is in and whatever its type, in `ontology.handling.withhold_sources`,
   the projection every node read passes through. `uprn` is not among them: a case's own `Location` keeps it
   (point 3a). A gazetteer's place still loses all seven (point 3a, unchanged).
2. **No node is matched on one of the six** for a request reader (`builders.match_any_field`, inside the
   traversal, so the rows, the extra row that says `more` and any count follow it): a reader is never sent one,
   so no search may answer on one, or a prefix search would rebuild it. A search whose fields are all among the
   six matches nothing; it does not fall back to every field. A gazetteer's place is still matched on its name
   alone (point 3b), and every other node by its name and the identifiers it is sent, a case's own `uprn` among
   them. This is how the reservation's "a Location matched on its name alone" is read here: a node is never
   matched on an identifier its reads withhold.
3. **The Conduit's own work keeps them** (`datasets is None`), and so does a read inside `sources_in_full` (a
   read written back, a gazetteer load), as in point 3a.
4. **A load's own match key is the load's work** (the orchestrator's ruling, 10 November 2026, on the lane
   review's question): `find_node` on a recipe's `match_on` (a Studio load's, and its Test's) matches its one
   named field unguarded, so a gazetteer re-loaded through the Studio by its `os_place_id` updates its places
   rather than doubling them. It runs as the reader's scoped principal, so it never reaches a node in a dataset
   the case does not read, and the Test's `referenced` count counts only nodes the reader may see; the node it
   reaches comes back without the six, as every node read does. The Test's preview of a node the file would
   create is the uploader's own file, not a node read, and keeps the file's values. Proved by
   `tests/ingest/test_gazetteer_only_ids_withheld_everywhere_live.py::test_a_load_s_match_reaches_no_node_the_reader_cannot_see`.
   A matched existing node in the Test's answer is the Test's to pass through `withhold_sources` as well (a
   carry to the studio lane).
5. **Amendment 1's "Left" line on a gazetteer loaded through the Studio** ("is the case's data and keeps its
   identifiers on every read") **is closed by this amendment**, and the port's contract
   (`ports/graph.py`'s `search_nodes` and `suggest_nodes`) states the wider rule.

**Cost.** An analyst's own data loses those six identifiers in reads and searches (the owner's ruling, MORNING
item 11).

**Tests.** `tests/ontology/test_gazetteer_identifiers_withheld.py` (a case's own Location keeps its `uprn` and
loses the six; any type of node; the Conduit keeps them); `tests/adapters/graph_arcadedb/test_gazetteer_name_only_match.py`
(no node matched on one of the six; the Conduit matches them; a search by one alone matches nothing);
`tests/ingest/test_gazetteer_only_ids_withheld_everywhere_live.py` (over ArcadeDB, through the real routes and at
the adapter: a case's own Location found by neither `osm_id` nor `os_place_id`, by search or type-ahead, with
no `more`; the step a search on those alone is sent keeps no node, the Conduit's own read finding it; found by
its name and its `uprn`, and sent with its `uprn` alone; decision 4's load match). The match and the read each
shown red by its own plant at its call site, the unit cases too (`plants.md`).

**Built by:** the platform-b lane, after P6.

### ADR-147, Amendment 4 (10 November 2026) — the case's gazetteer panel as built (P6)

**Why.** Amendment 2's "Left, and why" says "The Glass has no control for a gazetteer yet". This is that control, built by platform-b as step P6, and that line of Amendment 2 is closed by it.

**Decisions.**
1. **Where, and for whom.** The map's controls draw the panel beside the place search ("Gazetteers in this
   case's dataset"). It lists each gazetteer of the case's dataset's unit by name, added or not, and never a
   count. Add and Remove are offered only to a person holding `run_pipelines`; anyone else sees the list and
   a line saying what changing it needs. The Conduit's routes refuse them all the same: the panel hides a
   control and grants nothing (rule 3).
2. **The dataset changed is the case's own,** read from the datasets the case reads
   (`GET /v1/investigations/{id}/datasets`). The GET of the gazetteers gains no field.
3. **The empty list's four reasons are told apart** from those datasets, each in words that name no dataset:
   the case reads none; it reads a composite or more than one; it reads a drawing; or no gazetteer is built
   for its unit (Admin › Maps).
4. **Refusals are said in the Glass's own words,** never the Conduit's text (rule 7). One answer covers a
   404 for an unknown gazetteer and one from the dataset's gate. A removal shows the Conduit's fixed words
   (`REMOVED_WORDS`), which give no count.
5. **A change keeps the keyboard user's place.** The pressed button stays focusable while the copy runs
   (seconds per thousand places, decision 2's measurement); a press meanwhile does nothing. A failed change
   reads the list again, as a copy that failed part way keeps its record.
6. **The place search follows.** An answer shown is asked again after an add or a remove, so it neither lists
   places no longer offered nor leaves out new ones.

**Tests.** `apps/workspace/src/map/gazetteers.test.ts` (the routes, the four empty cases, the words);
`src/map/MapControls.test.tsx` (`CaseGazetteerPanel`: names only, no change without the right, busy and
focus, the re-read, a case change, and `PlaceSearch`'s `asOf`); `keyboard/map-view.spec.ts` (add, the
search asked again, remove, and a panel offering no change, keyboard alone; the registry ids
`add-a-gazetteer-by-keyboard` and `remove-a-gazetteer-by-keyboard`); `a11y/every-harness.spec.ts`
(`map-view-harness.html`'s eight panel states, dark, light and GOV.UK).

**Left.** The places census (`test_place_routes.py`) does not see a client bound in `App.tsx`; a
non-entry route of a place is the orchestrator's carry.

**Built by:** the platform-b lane, as step P6.


### ADR-143, Amendment 7 (10 November 2026) — merging a drawn dataset as built (L3.9), with the owner's ruling on mapping the models

Status: built by the case lane at L3.9 under Prompt L. The owner ruled on mapping the models (10
November 2026): "The entity type matching should be resolved through the ingest studio where the type
is mapped to the types in the domain model." The other decisions the brief left open were taken as
recommended and are recorded here for the owner to overrule; the mechanism for the ruling (item 3) was
agreed with the orchestrator before it was built. Amendment 2 decisions 6 and 7 and Amendment 3 stand
except where this says so. Spec 03's *Merging a drawn dataset* and spec 01's *Merged into another
dataset* have the detail.

1. **One promotion.** A merge is L3.4's promotion (Amendment 5 decision 1) with the trigger `drawn_merge`,
   all or nothing, under the target's highest marking and promotion policy, reviewed in the target's
   *Analyst promotions* by its Authors holding `review_promotions`, never the merger. Its record's
   `layer_id` is the drawn dataset.
2. **Who** (Amendment 3 decision 2): `merge_datasets` on all four routes; the target must be a source
   dataset of the drawing's unit that the merger is an Author of (its home case's, teams included). Every
   other target, of whatever kind, is answered 404 `not_a_target`, alike. The merger reads the drawing as
   any reader does, through its home case (its Author shares it with them): nothing here widens what
   anyone reads.
3. **Map the models (the owner's ruling).** Each drawn type is mapped onto any type of the target's live
   model of its kind, as a Studio load's Map step maps onto the domain model, or onto none; for one mapped
   onto another type, each drawn property is placed in a property or identifier of that type, or not
   carried. The sheet proposes the same name where the target's model holds it, else none, saying why.
   - A type mapped onto its own name goes as before: the same element gains the target (rule 6).
   - An item mapped onto another type is written by the merge's load as a **new element** of that type
     in the target (an element's type is its store class, kept for good): its properties as placed, its
     handling its original's (never lower: the orchestrator's condition), its drawn provenance, grading
     and source kept whole (read as written back, `sources_in_full`, ADR-130 Amendment 2: its sources
     and its board as stored, not as the merger is shown them), its load id the merge's. A node's copy
     has an `inferred` `SAME_AS` back to its drawn original (`model_version` drawn_merge_retype) in **no
     dataset**: ADR-099 Amendment 2 decision 3 puts a `SAME_AS` in the datasets its records share, and the
     copy (the target) and its original (the drawing) share none. So no case reads it and neither is
     joined to the other at query time (rules 5 and 6); it is the load's record of where the copy came
     from, written past the stamping graph as the resolver writes a cross-dataset match, and reverted
     with it. A link retyped, or touching a retyped node, is written new with its ends resolved to the
     copies; a link retyped between two items that go in as themselves is refused, since a link of
     that type may be loaded between them already, which the adapter would merge it into and the
     revert would then revert (whether one is, is not the merger's to know: rule 3).
   - **Who it credits:** a copy keeps its original's drawn assertion whole (its drawer, `asserted_by`,
     its grading and source); it is created by the merger (`created_by`), under the merge's load; the
     retyping itself is recorded in the promotion's copies (`promotion_copies`) and in the audit.
   - Only an original the merger reads is copied: each copy is built from the element as read through
     them (the orchestrator's condition), so one above them is neither copied, counted nor named.
   - The sheet takes the mapping chosen so far (`?mapping=`, a JSON list of `TypeChoice`; 422
     `not_a_mapping` when it cannot be read), so Match offers each node's matches as it will go in, and
     the screen reads them again whenever the mapping changes, letting go of a chosen pair no longer
     offered.
   - A type outside the target's model, or a property outside the chosen type, refuses the merge (422
     `not_a_type`, `not_a_property`, as does two drawn properties placed in one; a drawn type or property
     chosen twice, `mapping_repeated`); a property not placed is said in the dry run (`not_carried`); a
     link of a case's own proposed type touching a retyped node is its item's problem (the model cannot
     say what it joins); a copy that breaks its
     new type's rules (a required property, the ends a link type joins) is its item's problem; an item of
     a type mapped onto none is left out with its reason, never refused for it; a picture or a board's
     *Same* or *Not the same* on a retyped node is left out with its reason, to be made again on the copy.
   - The copies are kept with the record (`promotion_copies`, written in the record's own transaction),
     with what the load wrote for each.
4. **Match.** Candidates are read through the merger scoped to the target alone, in the adapter (no
   filter after retrieval), so no node of another dataset or above the merger is offered, counted or
   ordered. A retyped node is looked for as its new type and its match written from its copy. A chosen
   match must be one offered now, of a drawn node that goes (422 `not_a_match`, alike for every reason).
   It is written in the load's own transaction as a `SAME_AS` that is `inferred` and scored
   (`model_version` drawn_merge), in the target, marked as the stricter of its ends and within the
   target's highest.
5. **Dry run** counts only what the merger may see (`retyped` among them: those going in as another
   type, not a link written new only for its end) and writes nothing; the screen
   asks for it again after any change, the mapping included, and offers *Merge* only after it (the route
   does not require it, as Amendment 5's delete).
6. **After the merge** (decision 7): the drawing's home case reads the target, and the drawn dataset
   read-only; its boards become views (drawing off, layout and sharing kept, the drawn nodes added to the
   selection); a merged view answers `annotations` read through each reader's own principal. One merge
   per drawing; one waiting at a time.
7. **Revert** is the promotion's operator command; for a drawn merge it also reverts, in its
   transaction, the merge's matches and its copies with their links and `SAME_AS` back, as a load's own
   writes are (`revert_elements`, never a refresh's withdrawal, which `restore_withdrawn` would bring
   back), refused while a link written since rests on a copy, as on a promoted node; then it puts the
   case back on the drawing and the views back to boards, and takes the reverted copies and links out
   of every case's working set (stored bodies are projected as stored), with the load revert's own
   reverter; without those stores it refuses. The mapping chosen is audited where it is chosen (the
   sheet and the merge); the copies, with the type each goes in as and what was written for it, by
   the merge, its approval and the revert.
8. **Across the stores:** before the graph commits, the matches' and copies' ids are kept and the
   drawing's one merge claimed (`merge_drawn`, the case moved in the same Postgres transaction); of two
   merges at once one commits, the other is refused with nothing written; a failed graph commit undoes
   the claim. Only the boards' becoming views follows the commit: a failure there is logged and leaves
   them boards, on which nothing is drawn (`drawing_merged`).
9. **Review:** a reviewer's *Details* list the matches and each retyped item (waiting: its original, with
   the type it goes in as; committed: its copy, each written element once), counted as shown, in the list
   as in *Details* whatever its status; an approval checks each again, and a match changed since, an
   original whose marking, properties or drawn assertion changed since, or a mapped type gone from the
   target's model rejects the merge (Amendment 5 decision 6: never left waiting), as does a target no
   longer one the drawing may go into (asked again as `targets()` asks it: a source dataset of the
   drawing's unit, not a gazetteer) and a copy the adapter refuses at the commit (`items_changed`,
   never a bare error); the reviewer is told which of these it was.
10. **One waiting at a time** is asked before the record is written, and is not atomic: two merges of
    one drawing sent at the same moment may both wait. That is enough, because neither is written
    before its commit, and the commit's claim (`merge_drawn`, item 8) lets one alone commit: the other
    is refused `already_merged` and recorded rejected, nothing written. A unique index on waiting
    drawn merges would make the wait atomic too; it is not added (no index on the hot `promotions`
    table from a lane, CARRIES row 22).
11. **The grading change** (Amendment 6; decision 11) regrades the copies too: they are drawn items in
    no board's registry, read from the committed merges' copies (`PromotionStore.committed_copies`,
    `scripts.grading_change.copies_reader`).

**Tests.** `tests/services/api/test_drawn_merge.py` (each check red by its plant: `process/lanes/case/
gates/L3.9-plants.txt`, 77 plants); the live store cases in `test_promotion_store.py` (the copies, and
their transaction), `test_case_views_store.py`, `test_datasets_store.py` (`gates/L3.9-live-plants.py`);
`tests/conformance/graph_port/test_promotion.py`'s merge transaction cases and the retyped copies' on
real ArcadeDB (a copy and a link onto it in the promotion's transaction, rolled back whole, the
`SAME_AS` back in no dataset read by no reader by id, among two nodes or by expanding, and their revert); `keyboard/drawn-merge.spec.ts`
(mapping a type by keyboard among them), `keyboard/views.spec.ts`; axe in every harness, the mapping
state included.

**Not done.** A copy carries no picture and no board decision of its original; a drawn property is placed
by name, one value to one property, with no transform (guided mode's Knowledge Adapters are not offered
here); a proposed link type of the drawing is mapped only by the name it reads as, and its refusal
when touching a retyped node has no test (none of the fixtures draws one). Found beside it, not L3.9's:
a board offers link types whose model requires a property (`ROLE_IN`'s `role`), which a drawn link
cannot carry, so the adapter refuses drawing one.

### ADR-146, Amendment 4 (9 November 2026) — L2.10 as built: team routing (a routed alert read by the team's members and the home case's Authors, in the queue's query, trends and packs), one queue, filters, the lead's hand-off and Suppress until…, Raise an alert…, What raises alerts, watched patterns on a schedule

Status: built by the rules lane in L2.10 (ADR-146 decisions 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8; Amendment 1; ADR-145
Amendment 5 points 5 and 6), reserved in `ADR_RESERVATIONS.md`. The decisions the lane took without a
question (Prompt L) are listed under *Decisions taken* in `process/lanes/rules/REPORT.md`, each for the
owner to overrule. ADR-146 and its Amendments 1 and 2 are unchanged except where this says so.

1. **Team routing, a rule 3 read (decision 8).** A sentence's *Alert goes to* may name a team
   (`RuleSentence.team = "team"`, `team_id` its role id, refused at the route when no such team
   exists, 409 `unknown_team`). Its alerts carry `alerts.routed_team`. Who reads one is decided in the
   query, never after it (`alerts.queue_scope`, `_routed_sql`): a case member who is in the team on
   this request (the custom role their token carries, `alerts.reader_teams`, never kept; so a member who
   leaves the team reads nothing routed to it from their next token, one already issued carrying the role
   until it expires, as ADR-145 Amendment 5 says of a token's lifetime;
   `test_a_member_whose_token_no_longer_carries_the_team_reads_nothing_routed_to_it`), or an Author
   of the home case of the alert's dataset (`AlertStore.answers_for`, the app's
   `alert_routing.answers_for_datasets`, read per read; unset, the team alone, fail closed). The same
   check holds wherever such an alert is shown: the queue's list, its counts, an alert's detail and
   address, triage writes (`set_queue_triage`, `set_suppression`), a pack's alert item
   (`AlertStore.routed_readable`, in `packs.readable`) and alert trends (the fact's audience
   `routed`, counted in its case for the team's members alone, never its deployer as an owner;
   `analytics_duckdb/alert_facts.py`, both adapters). **A routed alert writes no `Alert` node**
   (`sentence_rules.writes_no_alert_node`), as a rule just for its author writes none: the node would
   carry the finding's words to every member who may read its markings. "My team" (`my_team`), the
   label written before teams, changes nobody's reading and is offered only for a rule saved with it
   (gap map Q5 (B)). In trends the home case's Authors do not count a routed alert (the narrower
   answer; they read it in the queue).
2. **One queue (decision 1).** The inbox's routes (`GET …/alerts`, `GET …/alerts/{id}`) and its
   component are gone; *what fired it* (the hotlist's entry, to its owner alone, and each matched
   node's files and rows) is on the queue's explanation (`watch_routes.with_what_fired_it`), given
   only once the reader may see the whole alert. The kind `analyst` joins the queue's kinds; the gap
   map's kind-dependent places each take it. A scheduled run's notice (K11), never a queue kind and
   shown only by the inbox, is now shown nowhere in the place: the Studio's schedules are its home
   (a request to the studio lane).
3. **The queue's filters (decision 2), in the query.** `show`: *Mine* (given to the reader), *Team*
   (routed to one of their teams, or shared with their unit), *Unassigned*, each leaving out an
   alert suppressed today; *All* (the default) holds the suppressed too. `older_than_days` keeps those
   raised more than N days ago.
4. **The lead's tools (Amendment 1).** The team's acting lead (`custom_roles.acting_lead`: the cover
   through its last day, else the lead) gives one of the team's alerts to a member of the team who
   holds the case at Editor or above, by their own grant or the team's (audited `alert_handed_off`);
   no one else gives a team alert to another person. *Suppress until…* (`POST …/alert-queue/{id}/
   suppress`, `AlertSuppressInput`): the lead or cover alone, a reason, a day today or later and at
   most 90 days ahead, audited `alert_suppressed`; the status is unchanged, so the alert is counted
   open everywhere, and it ends by itself (`alert_queue.suppressed_today`). An alert taken back by a
   revert (closed with no outcome, G12) is marked apart in the queue.
5. **Raised by an analyst (decision 7).** `POST …/raised-alerts` (`investigate`, Editor):
   `analyst:case:<case>` worked in the case, or `analyst:dataset:<dataset>` raised into the dataset's
   home case, in the queue of the home case and of every case reading the dataset, closed by the home
   case's Authors alone (`alert_queue.dispose`'s `closer`, fail closed). Refused before anything is
   written: a Viewer (403); a dataset the case does not read, a layer, or one with no home case (409
   `dataset_not_writable`, `no_home_case`); an item the raiser may not read, as one that does not
   exist (404); a dataset alert citing an item that is not the dataset's own, a drawn item (409
   `not_the_datasets_own`). The Glass offers it in the query builder on the selected items, with the
   query's name as what found them; the selection bar's and a question's answer's are the case and
   questions surfaces' (requests).
6. **What raises alerts (decision 5).** `GET …/alert-sources`: the case's rules and the reader's own
   hotlists and watched patterns (another's watch is its owner's), each with its maker, dataset, owner,
   state, expiry, last fired, alerts in 30 days and the share closed as not of interest, counted from
   the reader's own queue (rule 7), and its alerts suppressed today beside it. Each person it shows
   (maker, owner, suppressor) is served by name (ADR-106 and its Amendment 1's shape:
   `owner_name`, `by_name`, read time, never stored), the directory asked only for the ids of the
   rows served; a routed rule's owner is its team, by name.
7. **Watches made in the Glass and run on a schedule (decision 4, G16).** *Watch for this* (the
   Inspector, on an entity carrying an identifier: a hotlist entry, reviewed in 90 days) and *Save as
   a watch* (the query builder, on a saved pattern: a watched pattern), offered where the place is.
   A watched pattern runs on its own schedule too (`every` daily by default at 06:00 Europe/London,
   weekly, or never; `PUT …/monitors/{id}/schedule`, its owner alone), one replica per slot, as its
   owner resolved afresh and confined to its dataset (`monitor_schedule.MonitorScheduleExecutor`,
   through the same guarded match a load uses, `evaluation.match_monitor_guarded`); an owner who can
   no longer sign in stops it. **A watch is matched within its dataset only while its owner still
   reaches it** (the orchestrator's L2.10 review, item 4): a level, by the case's own Viewer check,
   on a case reading the dataset (`watch_reach.owner_reaches_dataset_in`), asked for the owner before
   they are narrowed, for hotlists and watched patterns, on the schedule and on every load
   (`MonitorScheduleExecutor.reaches_dataset`; `evaluate_hotlists_for_entry`'s and
   `evaluate_monitors_for_entry`'s `reaches_dataset`). The route's loads are given it by
   `WatchReachDep`; the scheduled and folder-watched runs by `RecipeRunDeps.from_state`, which builds
   it from the state's own dataset and case stores; the command-line load by `RunResources`, which
   holds both. Narrowing the owner to the dataset alone would give back one they had lost. An owner
   who has lost it is matched over nothing, logged, and the slot is spent, the watch kept (a case
   given back runs it again). A load path given no check matches no watch with a dataset (fail
   closed, logged); none is, and `test_run_resources.py` fails if the command-line one is not.
8. **The carries.** A settle on a read path purges what it re-marked at once, published to the
   connected canvases (`alerts.settle_repoints` with `AlertStore.working_set`). Outside a load
   (`raise_committed`), a node that cannot be written in a read-only dataset or marked leaves the row
   raised without it, said in the audit (`read_only_dataset`, `unseen_referent`), unless the finding
   writes alongside (a screening hit), whose refusal stands. The daily KYC sweep catches per case and
   per customer, counts each failure and writes it to the rule's audit (`rule_evaluation_failed`,
   listed in *Changes*), and closes the day. A scheduled slot or a re-screening that fails part-way
   keeps and counts what it raised (`rule_evaluation.PartlyRaised`).
9. **The address's timing residual, ruled (the owner, 9 November 2026, relayed by the orchestrator):
   Amendment 2 point 6's question, option (a), accepted.** A refusal at `/v1/alerts/{id}` waits to the
   end of its 250 ms quantum; an alert whose evidence takes longer than one quantum to read is refused
   on a later quantum and can alone be told from a missing id. That residual is accepted as recorded,
   neither capped nor given a larger quantum: it applies only to alerts with unusually large evidence,
   measured as a 177 ms worst-case read at L2.9, and at L2.10 as a hidden alert's read of 253.9 ms
   without the wait, run beside `make ci` under load (rules lease, stack b; green re-taken alone). The
   guarantee is the one measured, no wider; a change to the quantum or a cap is a new amendment.

**Left, and why.** An alert's address answers 404 where the reader's case is not the alert's own: a
dataset alert read from another case on its dataset, and a watch alert a schedule raised (no case);
both are worked in the queue that lists them, and their address waits for an address that names the
reader's case (a later step). The selection bar's and a question's answer's *Raise an alert…* are the
case and questions surfaces' (requests).

**Tests that would fail (rule 12), each shown red first** (`process/lanes/rules/l2.10/RED_RECORD.md`):
`test_monitoring_queue.py`'s three routing cases on Postgres (red with the routed check opened at
`_routed_sql`'s own clause, its parameters kept, and with the Authors' clause read for any dataset);
`test_pack_alert_item.py::test_an_alert_routed_to_a_team_is_withheld_in_a_pack_from_a_reader_outside_it`
(red with the pack's check removed); the analytics suite's
`test_a_team_routed_alert_is_counted_for_the_teams_members_alone` (red with the owner clause left open
to `routed`, and with the routed clause gone; run on DuckDB, ClickHouse's half at the orchestrator's
`conformance-analytics`); the rule audit's
`test_typology_rules.py::test_a_routed_alerts_firing_is_withheld_from_the_rule_audit_outside_its_team`;
`test_team_lead_and_watches.py` (the real Authors read, the lead and cover, Suppress until…, the
hand-off, a dataset alert's close, the watch schedule and a Glass-made watch's reach, a routed rule's
run counts); `test_sentence_rules.py`'s routed sentence (red with the
node written); `test_raise_an_alert.py` (red with the drawn-item check and the dataset check removed);
`test_alert_evidence_withheld.py::test_the_inbox_is_gone`; `test_alert_runs_partly_raised.py`,
`test_read_path_purge.py`, `test_composite_monitors.py::test_one_failing_rule_never_stops_the_daily_sweep_whole`
and `test_alert_node_marking.py::test_after_a_commit_an_unreadable_referent_node_raises_the_row_without_its_node`;
`alerts/OneQueue.test.tsx` and `RulesPlaceQueue.test.tsx`; `keyboard/alerts.spec.ts` and
`keyboard/watch-panels.spec.ts`, each new case driven by keys alone (a native select by typing its

from the orchestrator's review: `test_monitoring_queue.py::test_what_raises_alerts_lists_only_the_readers_watches_and_counts_only_what_they_may_see`
(another's watch, a routed rule's count, a hidden alert's count, the names), and in
